## OpenCode (mcp+rules)

| Step | File | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| MCP | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` | `mcp.aletheia = {type: "local", command: [bun, mcp.mjs], enabled: true}` |
| Rules | `AGENTS.md` / `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` | managed block |

No hook or plugin is written. The official plugin page lists `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` and event names
(`session.idle`, `message.updated`, `tool.execute.after`, ...) but not the fields inside each event payload.
Reading a guessed field such as `event.properties.sessionID` would be fabrication, so the capability is
`mcp+rules`. A JSONC-only `opencode.jsonc` is refused rather than parsed as JSON. OpenCode is installed here;
no plugin was loaded by us.

Source: <https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/>, <https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/>,
<https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/> (fetched 2026-10-26).

## Claude Desktop (MCP only)

No hooks and no rules file. The config merge is documented and fixture-tested in
[docs/claude-desktop.md](claude-desktop.md). The Linux path is observed on this machine, not in the MCP
quickstart, and is marked UNVERIFIED.

## Rule hygiene

`aletheia rules lint [--dir path] [--tools a,b] [--json]` checks the store and the managed blocks before a sync.
It reports duplicate rules once per group, direct `always`/`never` contradictions with the same scope and
condition, a rule over 300 characters, an enabled set over 4,000 characters, instructions that ignore safety
(`ignore previous instructions`, `bypass security`, `rm -rf /`, ...), and text that matches the redaction
patterns (a secret). For every managed block that exists under the project directory or the user home it
compares the parsed bullets with the enabled store rules: a rule only in the file and a rule only in the store
are both drift, each with the file and line or the rule id. Each finding has a fix hint.

The check is a warning, not a gate: `rules sync` still runs. `--json` returns `{findings, checked}`. A file
without the managed-block markers is skipped, so a user's own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md text is never compared.

Stale rules are reported too: `stale_rule` is a warning with the fix hint "confirm or retire", raised when a rule's
evidence went stale or nobody confirmed it within the review window (`rules.reviewDays`, default 90). It is a flag:
the rule stays enabled and `rules sync` still writes it. See [docs/03](03-http-api.md) for the reasons.

`aletheia rules confirm <id>` records that a rule is still right (its last-confirmed date becomes now) and writes an
audit row. `aletheia rules retire <id>` turns a rule off without deleting it. `aletheia rules list [--stale]
[--older-than N]` prints each rule with its date, source and a `[re-check: ...]` marker.

## Where the tools disagree

`aletheia rules diff [--dir path] [--tools a,b] [--json]` (and `GET /api/hub/rules/diff`) compares each tool's managed
block with the store. Per file it lists rules only in the store (with the rule id), rules only in the file (with the
line), and rules whose wording differs (store text, file text and line), then a count of tools out of sync. It never
writes. A file without the managed-block markers is reported as not compared. The Rules page shows the same count.

## Plugin manifests

Written 2026-10-26 from the official pages below. Every manifest carries `"x-aletheia-verification":
"from-docs-only"`: it was parsed and its paths were resolved against this package, but no host was opened to
load it. `test/manifests.test.mjs` checks the JSON, the paths and the hook commands.

| Host | File | What it declares | Source (fetched 2026-10-26) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemini CLI | `gemini-extension.json` | metadata and an `mcpServers.aletheia` entry using `${extensionPath}/bin/mcp.mjs` and `cwd: ${extensionPath}` | <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/main/docs/extensions/reference.md> |

What was not written, and why:

- **Codex MCP entry**: the official page says the compatibility layout can use a root `.mcp.json` and that
  `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` remains supported, but it does not give the field table for the compatibility
  manifest or the local `.mcp.json` server shape. Only the hook field, which the page names explicitly, is
  written. The full compatibility schema is UNVERIFIED.
- **Qoder components**: the page documents `mcpServers` and `hooks` as manifest fields, but not a variable for
  the plugin root. A relative command would resolve against an unknown working directory, so no component is
  claimed. The metadata shape is verified.
- **Gemini hooks**: the reference says hooks live in `hooks/hooks.json` and are not in the manifest. No
  extension hook file is shipped; the existing installers write the host's own hook files.

No manifest claims a hook whose script is missing, and no path escapes the package.

## Transcript watcher

Tools without hooks can still be imported from their session files. `aletheia watch` polls the three verified
layouts, keeps a byte offset and turn counter per file in `~/.aletheia/watcher.db`, and imports only new lines:

```bash
aletheia watch --once
aletheia watch --interval 1000 --batch 50 --tool claude-code,command-code,codex
```

| Tool | Folder | Verified from |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl` | 2026-10-26 |
| Command Code | `~/.commandcode/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl` | 2026-10-26 |
| Codex CLI | `~/.codex/sessions/<year>/<month>/<day>/rollout-*.jsonl` | two real rollouts on this machine, 2026-10-26 |

The source files are opened read-only. A file that shrinks is re-read from zero. A line without a newline is
left for the next pass. A JSON line the parser does not recognise, and a line that is not JSON, are stored as a
`kind = "raw"` episode instead of being dropped. The polling loop is clamped to at least 1000 ms, takes a batch
size per file, and the CLI sets `nice 10`. Restarting resumes at the stored offset; a re-read is deduped by
`source_ref` and content hash.

## End-to-end test

`test/e2e-more-hosts.test.mjs` installs all six full-capability hosts into a temp HOME, reads the command back
from each config, pipes a recorded payload set through it, and checks rows, redaction and p95. On 2026-10-26:
2 tests pass, p95 1.24 to 2.48 ms per host (hook work only). This is the real installed command, not a call to
the adapter; it is still not the host application.

## Check hooks in a real session

The fixtures prove the installed hook command, not the host. To check a real session, use a throwaway HOME, a
throwaway project and a throwaway data directory so nothing touches the real `~/.aletheia`, `~/.claude` or
`~/.commandcode`:

```bash
root=$(mktemp -d /tmp/aletheia-hook-check.XXXXXX)
mkdir -p "$root/home" "$root/project"
cd "$root/project"
export HOME="$root/home"
export ALETHEIA_DATA_DIR="$root/data"
export ALETHEIA_PORT=37890
aletheia install command-code --write
aletheia install claude-code --write
aletheia install codex --write
```

Start one short session in Command Code, Claude Code or Codex CLI in this project with the same `HOME`, send one
prompt and one file-reading tool call, then end the session. Codex requires the non-managed hooks to be reviewed
once with `/hooks` before they run. Run the checker on the data directory it wrote:

```bash
bun scripts/hook-check.mjs "$ALETHEIA_DATA_DIR" --tool command-code
bun scripts/hook-check.mjs "$ALETHEIA_DATA_DIR" --tool claude-code
bun scripts/hook-check.mjs "$ALETHEIA_DATA_DIR" --tool codex
```

`scripts/hook-check.mjs` opens `hub.db` read-only and prints the sessions seen, events per hook type, the first
and last timestamp, whether any stored text still matches a redaction pattern (reported as a row and column, never
the secret), whether the spool is empty, and a PASS/FAIL per expected event. It exits 1 on any FAIL.

What a real session captures per tool:

| Tool | Captured | Not captured |
|---|---|---|
| claude-code | SessionStart context (injected, no stored row), UserPromptSubmit (prompt), PostToolUse (tool event), Stop and SessionEnd (summary) | nothing in its five-event set |
| command-code | SessionStart context (injected, no stored row), PostToolUse (tool event), Stop (session end) | UserPromptSubmit and SessionEnd: Command Code has no such hooks, so prompts and session-end summaries are not captured |
| codex | SessionStart context (injected, no stored row), UserPromptSubmit (prompt), PostToolUse (tool event), Stop and SessionEnd (summary) | nothing in its five-event set |

Command Code has no `UserPromptSubmit` or `SessionEnd` hook, so the checker marks those two events "not installed"
instead of FAIL. `SessionStart` injects context but stores no row, so it is reported as context-only and cannot be
confirmed from the database. For Claude Code and Codex, the checker counts the summary memory as the Stop/SessionEnd
signal and falls back to the session-end table when that has rows and there is no summary.

# Migrate from claude-mem to Aletheia


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) can copy your claude-mem history into its own store with one command, `aletheia import claude-mem`. The import opens the claude-mem database read-only, so your old memory stays where it is.

This page covers the import, what maps to what, running both tools side by side, switching the Claude Code hook, and rolling back.

## Import your claude-mem history

Run the importer. With no flags it reads `~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db`, the default database path in the claude-mem installation page (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation, fetched 2026-10-29).

```bash
aletheia import claude-mem
```

The command prints how many rows it added and how many it skipped. This output comes from a small test database (2 observations, 1 summary, 1 prompt) in a temporary home folder, not from real data.

```json
{
  "observations": {
    "added": 2,
    "skipped": 0
  },
  "summaries": {
    "added": 1,
    "skipped": 0
  },
  "prompts": {
    "added": 1,
    "skipped": 0
  }
}
```

Run it again and every row is skipped. The import is idempotent: the store drops a memory when a memory with the same project, kind, title and text already exists.

```bash
aletheia import claude-mem
# "observations": { "added": 0, "skipped": 2 } ... "prompts": { "added": 0, "skipped": 1 }
```

### Flags

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--path <file>` | Read a database at another path. The default is `~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db`, or the value of `CLAUDE_MEM_DB`. |
| `--no-prompts` | Skip the `user_prompts` table. Observations and summaries are still imported. |
| `--project <name>` | Import only rows whose project is `<name>`. |

A missing file stops the command with `No claude-mem database at <path>.` The command prints a stack trace after that line; the message is the part to read.

### Import from the dashboard

Open the dashboard, go to the Knowledge tab, click **Import and export**, then click **Import from claude-mem**. The section appears only when the database file exists. I checked these labels in a real browser against a temporary server.

### Schema check

Before it reads any row, the importer checks that the tables `sdk_sessions`, `observations`, `session_summaries` and `user_prompts` exist and have the columns it needs. If claude-mem changes its schema, the import stops with a message that names the missing table or column, instead of importing nothing. Aletheia's tests use a synthetic database with the table shapes of claude-mem 15.2.0. I did not run the importer against a real claude-mem 15.x database for this page.

## What maps to what

| claude-mem | Aletheia memory | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `observations` row | kind `observation` | Keeps type (`bugfix`, `feature`, `refactor`, `change`, `discovery`, `decision`; other types pass through), title, subtitle, narrative, facts, concepts, and the union of files read and modified. |
| `session_summaries` row | kind `summary`, type `note` | The fields request, investigated, learned, completed, next steps and notes become one text with a bold label per field. An empty summary is skipped. |
| `user_prompts` row | kind `prompt` | The prompt text becomes the title and the body. |

Every imported memory keeps its original timestamp, the project name, the session id and the tool name from `platform_source` (default `claude`). The `origin` field records the source row, for example `claude-mem:obs:3`.

The importer reads only those four tables. Every other table in the claude-mem database is ignored, and so are claude-mem's settings and its vector index. claude-mem's installation page lists `uv` as the provider of Python for Chroma's embedding service (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation, fetched 2026-10-29). Aletheia does not import vectors. Imported memories are found by keyword search unless you install the optional embedding package and run `aletheia embed`.

### The import redacts secrets

The store redacts every text it saves, imports included, so a fake AWS key id or a `password=` value in claude-mem's database is stored as `[redacted:...]`. Versions before this change copied the text exactly. If you imported with an older version, redact those rows in place:

```bash
aletheia scrub            # count the rows that redaction would change
aletheia scrub --apply    # redact them (back up hub.db first)
```

Redaction is pattern based, so check what you imported before you rely on it:

```bash
aletheia search "password"
aletheia search "AKIA"
```

Remove a memory you do not want. Report first, then apply:

```bash
aletheia erase --id 12
aletheia erase --id 12 --apply
```

Fact extraction redacts text again before it sends it to a model provider. See [Model providers](model-providers.md) for what is and is not redacted on each path.

## Run claude-mem and Aletheia side by side

The two tools keep separate stores.

- Aletheia writes only under its data directory (`~/.aletheia` by default). It listens on port 37790.
- claude-mem keeps `~/.claude-mem/`. Its worker port defaults to `37700 + (uid % 100)` (https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting, fetched 2026-10-29). The two defaults collide only when `uid % 100` is 90. Change Aletheia's port with `ALETHEIA_PORT`.
- Aletheia never writes to the claude-mem database. It opens the file with `readonly` and `query_only`. In my test the file's checksum was identical before and after two imports.

I did not test an import while claude-mem was writing to its database. Run the import while claude-mem is idle.

If both tools have hooks in Claude Code, each one captures the same prompts and each one adds its own context block at session start. Expect duplicate context until you turn one off.

## Switch the Claude Code hook to Aletheia

1. Preview the install. Without `--write` the command is a dry run and writes nothing.

   ```bash
   aletheia install claude-code
   ```

   ```text
   Claude Code (claude-code) — full, mcp-verified
     write  mcp      ~/.claude.json  (mcpServers.aletheia)
     write  hooks    ~/.claude/settings.json  (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd)
     write  rules    ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md  (0 rules)
   ...
   Dry run: nothing was written. Add --write to apply.
   ```

2. Apply it. Each changed file gets a timestamped backup.

   ```bash
   aletheia install claude-code --write
   ```

   The installer adds its own hook entries and leaves other hooks alone. In a test, a hook I had put in `settings.json` by hand was still there after install and after uninstall.

3. Turn off the claude-mem plugin so only one tool captures. Claude Code's documentation describes `/plugin disable` inside a session and `claude plugin disable <name>@<marketplace>` on the command line (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins, fetched 2026-10-29). On the machine where I wrote this page, `claude plugin list` shows the plugin as `claude-mem@thedotmack`:

   ```bash
   claude plugin disable claude-mem@thedotmack
   ```

   I did not run this command, because `claude plugin list` already showed that plugin as disabled, and I did not check the exact screens of the `/plugin` panel. If you installed claude-mem with `npx claude-mem install` instead of the plugin marketplace, the plugin id may not exist. Follow claude-mem's own documentation to remove its hooks. Whether disabling the plugin also stops claude-mem's background worker is UNVERIFIED; check the worker port from your claude-mem settings.

4. Confirm the install.

   ```bash
   aletheia doctor
   aletheia install claude-code --verify
   ```

   `doctor` should show `hooks claude-code  5/5`. `--verify` compares the files with the install record. These checks read configuration files. They do not prove a hook ran. Start a new Claude Code session, send one prompt, then run `aletheia search <word from the prompt>`.

   Hooks ran in real sessions of Claude Code (two days of use), Command Code (one short session) and Codex CLI (one interactive session), one user on one machine.

## What you keep and what you lose

You keep:

- Observations, summaries and prompts as searchable memories, in the Knowledge tab, in `aletheia search` and through the MCP `search` tool.
- Your claude-mem database, untouched.

You do not get from the import:

- claude-mem's vector index. Aletheia's vector search is optional and builds its own vectors.
- Tool-use records and work-state entries. The importer does not read those tables.
- Facts. Imported observations are not turned into facts, because fact extraction reads only summaries and notes.
- claude-mem's own viewer and modes. Aletheia has its own dashboard.

## Roll back

1. Remove Aletheia's entries from Claude Code. This is a dry run until you add `--write`, and it removes only the entries listed in Aletheia's install record.

   ```bash
   aletheia uninstall claude-code --write
   ```

2. Turn the claude-mem plugin back on.

   ```bash
   claude plugin enable claude-mem@thedotmack
   ```

3. Remove the imported memories if you want a clean slate. Pick the project name, check the report, then apply.

   ```bash
   aletheia erase --project shop
   aletheia erase --project shop --apply
   ```

Nothing in these steps changes the claude-mem database.

## Next steps

- [Write rules once](write-rules-once.md) - turn the rules you repeat in every tool into one list.
- [Claude Code](../tools/claude-code.md) - what the Claude Code installer writes and what was checked.
- [Aletheia vs claude-mem](../compare/aletheia-vs-claude-mem.md) - a sourced comparison of the two tools.
- [Backup, export and import](backup-export-import.md) - copy your new store to another machine.
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) - fixes for the problems people hit after an install.

---

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/write-rules-once.html

# Write your AI coding rules once and sync them to every tool


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) keeps your standing rules in one list and writes them into the instruction file each AI coding tool reads, such as `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`. You edit the list in one place, preview the result, and then write the files.

This guide walks through the full loop with the CLI and the dashboard. Every command output below came from a temporary home folder and project folder, not from real files.

## Step 1: Add rules

Add a rule from the command line. The text is the rule. Add `--when` for a rule that applies only in a situation.

```bash
aletheia rules add "Run the tests before you commit"
aletheia rules add "Use the repo's formatter" --when "you edit a .mjs file"
```

```text
Added r_a188fedbf2.
Added r_daf40b0979.
```

Adding the same rule again prints `Already there (<id>).` and changes nothing.

In the dashboard, open the Rules tab and click **Add a rule**. The dialog has these fields:

- What the tool should do (the rule text)
- When (optional)
- Applies to: Everywhere, One project, or One situation
- Only for these tools (leave all unticked for every tool)

List your rules at any time:

```bash
aletheia rules list
```

```text
on  r_a188fedbf2  Run the tests before you commit  [everywhere]  (added 2026-10-29, source: you, last confirmed 2026-10-29)
on  r_daf40b0979  When you edit a .mjs file: Use the repo's formatter  [everywhere]  (added 2026-10-29, source: you, last confirmed 2026-10-29)
```

Rules live in the Aletheia database. The tool files are an output, not the source. Editing a tool file by hand does not change the list.

## Step 2: Choose a scope

A rule has a scope and an optional tool filter.

- **Everywhere** puts the rule under the heading `## Everywhere`.
- **One project** puts it under `## In <project name>`.
- **One situation** puts it under a heading with the name you give.
- **Only for these tools** limits the rule to the tools you tick. A rule with no tool filter goes to every tool.

The scope sets the heading. It does not filter by folder. In a test, a rule scoped to the project `shop` appeared under `## In shop` in the `AGENTS.md` of a different folder. A rule limited to `codex` was missing from the `CLAUDE.md` that was written in the same run.

The CLI `rules add` command makes Everywhere rules. Set a project scope or a tool filter in the dashboard dialog, or import rules from a file that already has headings (Step 3).

## Step 3: Import the rules you already have

If your tools already have rule files, import them instead of retyping.

```bash
aletheia rules import --tool claude-code --dir /path/to/project
aletheia rules import --tool claude-code --global
```

```text
{
  "found": 3,
  "added": 3,
  "skipped": 0
}
```

The importer reads bullet lines (`- ...` or `* ...`). A `## Heading` above a bullet becomes the scope name, so the bullets under `## Testing` become rules in the situation `Testing`. A file with no heading gives Everywhere rules. Running the import again skips rules you already have.

Two limits to know:

- If the file already has an Aletheia managed block, the importer reads only the bullets inside the block. Your own bullets outside the block are not read.
- Rule ids are new on each hub. The same rule text gets a different id on another machine.

In the dashboard, use Rules, then **Import**: pick the tool, type a project folder (blank means the global file) and click **Import rules**.

## Step 4: Preview, diff and lint

Nothing is written until you ask. Two read-only commands show where the files and the list disagree.

```bash
aletheia rules diff --dir /path/to/project --tools claude-code,codex
```

```text
claude-code  /path/to/project/CLAUDE.md  differs
  only in store  r_8358622fa2  Always run bun test before a commit
  ...
codex  /path/to/project/AGENTS.md  differs
  only in file   /path/to/project/AGENTS.md:10  Prefer tabs
  text differs   r_a188fedbf2 vs /path/to/project/AGENTS.md:8
    store: Run the tests before you commit
    file:  Run all tests before you commit
2 tools out of sync.
```

`rules diff` compares only files that contain the managed block. A file without the block is reported as unmanaged, not as a difference. Add `--json` for machine-readable output. The command exits with code 0 even when files differ.

`rules lint` checks the list and the managed blocks for hygiene problems:

```bash
aletheia rules lint --dir /path/to/project --tools claude-code,codex
```

```text
r_1732204248  drift_store_only  Rule r_1732204248 is in the store but missing from the managed block in .../CLAUDE.md.
  fix: Run aletheia rules sync --write for that tool.
file:.../AGENTS.md:3  drift_file_only  The managed block in .../AGENTS.md has a rule the store does not: "Prefer tabs".
  fix: Add it in the Rules view or run aletheia rules sync --write to restore the block.
```

The checks, from [the lint code](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/rule-lint.mjs): duplicate rules, direct contradictions (same scope, opposite polarity), a rule over 300 characters, an enabled set over 4,000 characters, text that tells an agent to ignore safety, a secret inside a rule, a stale rule, and drift between the store and a managed block. The command exits with code 1 when it finds anything, so you can run it in CI. With no findings it prints `No findings.`

## Step 5: Write the files

Write global files (in your home folder) or project files (in one folder). Add `--write` to apply; without it the command is a dry run.

```bash
aletheia rules sync --tools claude-code,codex --global --write
aletheia rules sync --tools claude-code,codex --dir /path/to/project --write
```

```text
- claude-code: /path/to/project/CLAUDE.md — 5 rules, written (backup /path/to/project/CLAUDE.md.aletheia-2026-10-29T19-47-38-813Z.bak)
- codex: /path/to/project/AGENTS.md — 5 rules, written
```

Run the same command again and each line ends with `already up to date`.

Always pass `--tools`. Without it, `rules sync` targets all ten entries in the tool registry, including `copilot`, `aider` and `agents-md`. The tool ids and their files:

| Tool id | Project file | Global file |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-code` | `CLAUDE.md` | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` |
| `command-code` | `AGENTS.md` | `~/.commandcode/AGENTS.md` |
| `codex` | `AGENTS.md` | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` |
| `gemini-cli` | `GEMINI.md` | `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` |
| `cursor` | `.cursor/rules/aletheia.mdc` | none |
| `windsurf` | `.windsurf/rules/aletheia.md` | `~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/global_rules.md` |
| `opencode` | `AGENTS.md` | `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` |
| `copilot` | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | none |
| `aider` | `CONVENTIONS.md` | none |
| `agents-md` | `AGENTS.md` | none |

A tool with no global file is skipped, and the command prints a line such as `- cursor: Cursor has no global rules file.`

In the dashboard, open Rules, then **Write to tools**. Tick the tools, choose **A project folder** (type its absolute path) or **Global**, click **Preview changes**, then **Write files**. The page asks you to confirm before it writes. The Rules page also shows a line such as `1 tool out of sync with these rules` when a file has drifted.

## What the generated file looks like

This is the `AGENTS.md` that `rules sync --tools codex` wrote after the steps above. The same block goes into `CLAUDE.md`.

```markdown
# Rules

Managed by aletheia-mem. Edit them in the Rules page; this block is rewritten on sync.

## Everywhere

- Run the tests before you commit
- When you edit a .mjs file: use the repo's formatter

## In shop

- Deploy only from the staging branch

## Testing

- Always run bun test before a commit
- Never mock the database in integration tests
```

Cursor gets a whole file that Aletheia owns, with the front matter Cursor documents:

```markdown
---
description: Standing rules managed by aletheia-mem
alwaysApply: true
---

...
```

Windsurf's project file is also written whole, with `trigger: always_on` front matter. Global scope always uses the block form.

Rules for Cursor, Gemini CLI and Windsurf: config written from docs, not tested on a real install. The files above are written and checked in temporary folders; see [the rules targets record](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/docs/verification/rules-targets.md).

## Keep rules fresh

A rule can go stale. Aletheia flags it and keeps syncing it until you decide.

```bash
aletheia rules list --stale
aletheia rules confirm r_a188fedbf2
aletheia rules retire r_1732204248
```

```text
Confirmed r_a188fedbf2 on 2026-10-29. The rule is unchanged.
Retired r_1732204248: turned off, not deleted. Turn it back on in the Rules page.
```

A rule is flagged when its evidence changed after the last confirmation, or when nobody confirmed it within the review window (90 days by default). Confirm a rule to restart the clock. Retire a rule to turn it off. A retired rule stays in the list and leaves the files on the next sync. In a test, the managed block went from 5 rules to 4 after one `retire` and one `sync --write`.

## Safety

- Only the managed block changes. Text outside the `<!-- aletheia:rules:begin -->` and `<!-- aletheia:rules:end -->` markers is left alone. A hand-written `CLAUDE.md` with notes and bullets kept all of them.
- Every write that changes an existing file first copies it to `<file>.aletheia-<timestamp>.bak`.
- Do not edit inside the block. The next sync rewrites it. In a test, a hand-edited line and a hand-added line inside the block were both replaced.
- A file with no markers gets a new block appended at the end.
- `aletheia uninstall <tool>` removes the block with the other entries that tool's installer wrote.
- Rules are plain text that every tool will follow. `rules lint` flags a rule that tells an agent to ignore safety or that contains a secret. Read the file before you commit it.

## Next steps

- [Rules](../concepts/rules.md) - how rules, scopes and evidence fit together.
- [Installer reference](../25-installers.md) - what each tool's installer writes, with sources.
- [Tools overview](../tools/overview.md) - which tools were checked on a real install.
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) - the Rules page is empty after an install.

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/backup-export-import.html

# Back up, export and move Aletheia memory between machines


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) stores everything in one SQLite database, `hub.db`, in `~/.aletheia` by default. You can export your memories and rules as a portable file, copy the database itself, or keep two machines in step with sync.

Each method keeps different things, so pick by what you need to move.

## Pick a method

| Method | What it carries | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| Export bundle (`.jsonl`) | Memories and rules | You move to another machine or tool and want a small, readable file. |
| Export Markdown | Rules and notes, as text | You want to paste your memory into a chat tool or read it. |
| Copy `hub.db` | Everything in the database: memories, facts, episodes, settings, dismissals | You want an exact backup or a full move. |
| Sync | Live changes between devices | You use two machines every day. See [Sync](../29-sync.md). |

## Export a bundle

```bash
aletheia export --out bundle.jsonl
aletheia export --project shop --out shop.jsonl
aletheia export --events --out everything.jsonl
```

Without `--out` the bundle goes to the terminal. The first line is a manifest; then comes one line per memory and one per rule. This is the manifest line from a test hub:

```json
{"type":"manifest","format":"aletheia-bundle","version":1,"exportedAt":"2026-10-29T19:46:20.267Z","project":null,"counts":{"memories":5,"rules":2}}
```

What the bundle holds, from [the export code](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/store.mjs):

- Memories: project, kind, type, title, subtitle, text, facts, concepts, files, tool, session id, pinned flag, origin and creation time.
- Rules: scope, text, enabled flag, tool filter and source. `--project` filters memories only. Every export contains all rules.
- Tool events (`kind` event) only with `--events`. They are left out by default.
- Prompts are included by default.

What it does not hold: facts, episodes, settings, sync data, and which memories you dismissed. A dismissed memory is still exported. In a test, `aletheia dismiss 1` followed by an export still showed all 5 memories.

In the dashboard, open Knowledge, click **Import and export**, then **Export bundle (.jsonl)** or **Export Markdown**.

## Export Markdown

```bash
aletheia export --format markdown --out memory.md
```

The file starts with your enabled rules, then one section per project, newest first. It skips events and prompts and lists at most 500 items per project. It is for reading and pasting. It is not an import format.

## Import a bundle

```bash
aletheia import bundle bundle.jsonl
```

```json
{
  "memories": {
    "added": 5,
    "skipped": 0
  },
  "rules": {
    "added": 2,
    "skipped": 0
  },
  "errors": []
}
```

Import is idempotent. Run it again and every row is skipped, because the store compares project, kind, title and text.

Memory ids and rule ids are new in the target hub. The importer stops with `Not an aletheia bundle` when the first line is not a manifest, and with a version message when the bundle is newer than the program. A bad line inside the file is reported in `errors` and the rest still imports.

In the dashboard, use **Import bundle** in the same panel. After a large import, run:

```bash
aletheia optimize
```

It rebuilds the full-text index segments. Search stays correct without it. The step keeps query time low.

## Copy hub.db safely

`hub.db` runs in write-ahead log (WAL) mode. Recent writes can live in `hub.db-wal`, not in `hub.db`. A copy of `hub.db` alone can be missing everything.

I checked this on a test hub after a few commands. The data directory held:

```text
hub.db       4096 bytes
hub.db-shm  32768 bytes
hub.db-wal  1079472 bytes
```

A copy of `hub.db` alone opened with `no such table: memories`. SQLite's documentation says the same: the WAL file is part of the database and must stay with it when you copy or move it; a database separated from its WAL can lose committed transactions or become corrupt (https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html, fetched 2026-10-29).

Do not assume that stopping the server empties the WAL. In my test the CLI commands had all exited and the `-wal` file was still there. Use one of these methods.

### Method 1: copy all three files together

Stop the server and every hook-driven tool, then copy `hub.db`, `hub.db-wal` and `hub.db-shm` as a set. In the test, a copy of all three opened with all rows present.

```bash
cp ~/.aletheia/hub.db ~/.aletheia/hub.db-wal ~/.aletheia/hub.db-shm /backup/
```

### Method 2: make a consistent copy with SQLite

These work while the server runs. I ran each one on a test hub and the copy held every row; `PRAGMA integrity_check` returned `ok`.

```bash
sqlite3 ~/.aletheia/hub.db ".backup /backup/hub.db"
sqlite3 ~/.aletheia/hub.db "VACUUM INTO '/backup/hub.db'"
```

Aletheia does not ship the `sqlite3` program. If you do not have it, Bun can run `VACUUM INTO`:

```bash
bun -e 'import { Database } from "bun:sqlite"; new Database(process.argv[1], { readonly: true }).exec(`VACUUM INTO "${process.argv[2]}"`)' ~/.aletheia/hub.db /backup/hub.db
```

`VACUUM INTO` needs a target that does not exist yet, or one that is empty (https://www.sqlite.org/lang_vacuum.html, fetched 2026-10-29). The `.backup` command is documented in the SQLite shell page (https://www.sqlite.org/cli.html, fetched 2026-10-29).

### Method 3: checkpoint, then copy

`aletheia migrate` uses this approach when it backs up before a schema change: it runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` and then copies the main file. You can do the same by hand:

```bash
sqlite3 ~/.aletheia/hub.db "PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);"
cp ~/.aletheia/hub.db /backup/hub.db
```

In the test the command printed `0|0|0` and the copy held every row. A write that lands between the checkpoint and the copy is not in the copy.

### Related files

The data directory also holds `sync.db`, `team.db`, `alerts.db`, `watcher.db`, `erasure.key` and folders for spool, erasure receipts and models. Copy them only if you use those features. Keep `erasure.key` private: it signs erasure receipts.

## Move to another machine

1. Install the same or a newer version of Aletheia on the new machine. A database with a newer schema than the program stops with `This database is schema v<N>; this build understands up to v<M>.` Check a database with `aletheia migrate --dry-run`.
2. Move the data with a bundle (see "Export a bundle" and "Import a bundle" above) or with a copy of the database files.
3. Run `aletheia doctor`. It checks the data folder and database file permissions (folder `0700`, files `0600`) and reports loose ones.
4. Install your tools again. Do not copy `install-manifest.json` or `aletheia.bundle.mjs` from the old machine. The hook commands in tool settings hold absolute paths to Bun and to that bundle.

   ```bash
   aletheia install claude-code --write
   ```

5. Write your rules into the tool files again. See [Write rules once](write-rules-once.md).

## Erase memory and keep a receipt

`aletheia erase` removes rows and signs a receipt. It reports first. It deletes only when you add `--apply`.

```bash
aletheia erase --project shop
```

```text
Erasure report for project "shop"

  memories              5  ids 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  observations          0
  episodes              0
  facts                 0
  summaries             0
  rule suggestions      0

Nothing was deleted. Add --apply to erase, export first with --export <file>.
Report only. Add --apply to erase.
```

Pick what to erase with `--project <name>`, `--id 12,fact:3` or `--before 2026-01-31`. Apply with an export and a receipt path:

```bash
aletheia erase --project shop --apply --export pre-erase.jsonl --receipt receipt.json
aletheia erase verify receipt.json
```

```text
Pre-erase export: pre-erase.jsonl
Erased {"memories":5,"observations":0,"episodes":0,"facts":0,"summaries":0,"ruleSuggestions":0}; sync entities purged 0, local sync rows 0.
Receipt: receipt.json
Verify: aletheia erase verify receipt.json
ok receipt.json
```

Without `--export` and `--receipt`, the files go to `erasure-exports/` and `erasure-receipts/` in the data directory. The receipt lists counts and ids, never content, and carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature made with `erasure.key`. Verification needs that key.

Limits:

- Erase does not delete rules. It does delete rule suggestions for the scope you pick.
- It deletes rows. I found no `VACUUM` or secure-delete step in the erase code. SQLite's `secure_delete` setting is normally off, so deleted text can stay in free pages of the file until they are reused (https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html, fetched 2026-10-29). If you must remove text from the file, make a `VACUUM INTO` copy after the erase and use that copy.
- A backup or bundle you made earlier still holds the data.

## Next steps

- [Sync](../29-sync.md) - keep two machines in step instead of moving files.
- [Privacy and redaction](../concepts/privacy.md) - what is redacted before it is stored.
- [Run as a service](run-as-a-service.md) - stop and restart the server around a copy.
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) - database locked, corruption and permission problems.

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/run-as-a-service.html

# Run Aletheia as a background service (systemd, launchd, Docker)


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) needs its server running to serve the dashboard, the REST API and the background extraction worker. `aletheia service install` writes a systemd user unit on Linux or a launchd plist on macOS so that the server starts on its own. It only writes the file. You start the service yourself.

Hooks and the CLI do not need the server. They open `hub.db` directly. The server matters for the dashboard, the HTTP API and extraction.

## What the service command does

```bash
aletheia service status
aletheia service install [--write] [--cpu-quota 25%] [--memory-max 512M]
aletheia service uninstall [--write]
```

- `install` and `uninstall` are dry runs until you add `--write`.
- The command writes a text file and a record, `service-manifest.json`, in the data directory. It never calls `systemctl` or `launchctl`.
- The output says `"verification": "from-docs-only"`. The generated unit was written from documentation. I did not start a generated unit for this page. Run the commands below on your own machine and read what they print.
- Windows is not covered. The command prints `Windows auto-start is not supported. Start aletheia-server manually or through Task Scheduler.`

## Linux: a systemd user unit

Preview the unit. The paths below are placeholders. Your output shows your own Bun path and package path, as absolute paths.

```bash
aletheia service install
```

```json
{
  "platform": "linux",
  "supported": true,
  "kind": "systemd",
  "label": "aletheia.service",
  "file": "/home/you/.config/systemd/user/aletheia.service",
  "content": "[Unit]\nDescription=Aletheia memory hub (loopback)\n...",
  "verification": "from-docs-only",
  "dryRun": true,
  "changed": true,
  "note": "Dry run: nothing was written. Add --write to apply."
}
```

Write it, then start it with systemd:

```bash
aletheia service install --write
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now aletheia
```

The `systemctl` lines are the ones in [the operations notes](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/docs/07-operations.md). The service command does not run them.

### The unit the command writes

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Aletheia memory hub (loopback)
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/home/you/.bun/bin/bun /path/to/package/bin/aletheia-server.mjs
Restart=on-failure
Nice=10
Environment=ALETHEIA_HOST=127.0.0.1
Environment=ALETHEIA_DATA_DIR=/home/you/.aletheia
Environment=ALETHEIA_HUB_DB=/home/you/.aletheia/hub.db
Environment=ALETHEIA_PORT=37790

# Defaults (override with --cpu-quota / --memory-max):
# CPUQuota=50%
# MemoryMax=1G

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
```

Three things to know:

- The port, data directory and database path are taken from the shell that ran the command. In a test, running the command with `ALETHEIA_PORT=37999` wrote `ALETHEIA_PORT=37999`, and running it again without that variable changed the file back to 37790 and made a backup.
- `ExecStart` holds the absolute path of Bun and of the server script at install time. If you move Bun or reinstall the package in a new place, run `aletheia service install --write` again, then `systemctl --user daemon-reload`.
- The unit sets only those four `Environment` lines. Provider settings such as `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER` are not copied. Add them with `systemctl --user edit aletheia`, or edit the file and run `daemon-reload`. See [Model providers](model-providers.md).

### CPU and memory limits

Pass limits at install time. They become `CPUQuota=` and `MemoryMax=` lines in the `[Service]` section.

```bash
aletheia service install --write --cpu-quota 25% --memory-max 512M
```

Without these flags the two lines are written as comments that show the defaults (50% and 1G). Those defaults are not applied until you pass a flag. `Nice=10` is always set. The two flags apply to the Linux unit only. The macOS plist has no limit keys.

### Check it and read logs

```bash
aletheia service status
systemctl --user status aletheia
journalctl --user -u aletheia -f
```

`aletheia service status` prints the plan and whether the unit file exists (`"installed": true`) plus the stored record. It does not ask systemd whether the service is running. Use `systemctl --user status aletheia` for that. The unit sets no log file, so output goes to systemd's default destination for the user service, which `journalctl --user -u aletheia` reads.

For a quick liveness check, ask the server directly:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:37790/healthz
```

```json
{"status":"ok","db":{"ok":true,"detail":"quick_check ok"},"fts":{"ok":true,"detail":"FTS5 query answered"},"vectors":{"memories":0,"facts":0},"model":"Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5"}
```

A `503` with `"status":"error"` means the database check or the search-index check failed. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

### Remove the unit

```bash
systemctl --user disable --now aletheia
aletheia service uninstall --write
systemctl --user daemon-reload
```

The uninstall copies the unit to `aletheia.service.aletheia-bak-<timestamp>`, deletes it and deletes the record.

### The hand-written unit in the repository

A git checkout also has `scripts/aletheia.service`. It runs from the checkout (`WorkingDirectory=%h/Projects/aletheia-mem`, `ExecStart=%h/.bun/bin/bun bin/aletheia-server.mjs`, `ALETHEIA_PORT=37790`). Edit the paths to match your checkout, then copy it to `~/.config/systemd/user/`. Use it only if you run from a clone. The command above is the better choice for an installed package.

## macOS: a launchd plist

On macOS the command writes `~/Library/LaunchAgents/aletheia.plist`, label `com.aletheia.mem`. It sets `KeepAlive` to true and sends output to `<data dir>/aletheia.log`. The same four environment variables go into the plist. This is the program section:

```xml
<key>Label</key>
<string>com.aletheia.mem</string>
<key>ProgramArguments</key>
<array>
  <string>/Users/you/.bun/bin/bun</string>
  <string>/path/to/package/bin/aletheia-server.mjs</string>
</array>
<key>KeepAlive</key>
<true/>
```

I rendered this plist on Linux by asking the code for the macOS plan. I did not run it on a Mac. Apple's launchd documentation says launchd loads user agents from the `LaunchAgents` folder in the user's Library (https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/MacOSX/Conceptual/BPSystemStartup/Chapters/CreatingLaunchdJobs.html, fetched 2026-10-29). That page does not describe `launchctl` commands, and the command here does not run them. Load the agent the way Apple's `launchctl` manual describes, and read `<data dir>/aletheia.log` for output.

## Port conflicts

The server listens on port 37790. If another process holds it, the server stops with `EADDRINUSE`. Find the owner, or pick another port:

```bash
ss -ltnp | grep 37790
ALETHEIA_PORT=37791 aletheia-server
```

For a service, change the port with `ALETHEIA_PORT=37791 aletheia service install --write`, then restart. `aletheia doctor` checks the port in `ALETHEIA_PORT`, so set the same value in your shell when you run it.

## Restart after an upgrade

A running server keeps the old code in memory until you restart it.

```bash
npm install -g aletheia-mem@latest
systemctl --user restart aletheia
aletheia --version
aletheia install claude-code --write
```

The last command rebuilds the hook bundle that tools run. The installer rebuilds `aletheia.bundle.mjs` in the data directory only when the package sources are newer than the bundle. Repeat it for each tool you installed. If the package moved to a new path, run `aletheia service install --write` and `systemctl --user daemon-reload` as well.

## Docker

The repository has a `Dockerfile` and a `compose.yaml`. I did not run `docker build` or `docker compose` for this page. The repository's own test (`test/dockerfile.test.mjs`) only checks the text of the files, and its header says `docker build` is not run by the author.

What the files say:

- The image starts from `oven/bun:1.3.10-alpine`, creates a non-root user `aletheia`, and copies `bin`, `src`, `public`, `public-hub`, `prompts` and `vendor`.
- It sets `ALETHEIA_DATA_DIR=/data` and `ALETHEIA_PORT=37790`, declares `/data` as a volume, and runs `bun bin/aletheia-server.mjs`.
- The health check calls `http://127.0.0.1:37790/healthz` every 30 seconds with `wget`.
- No secret is baked in.
- `compose.yaml` uses `network_mode: host`, `restart: unless-stopped` and a named volume `aletheia-data` mounted at `/data`. Host networking works on Linux only. The server then binds `127.0.0.1` in the host's network, so only your machine reaches it.
- The comments in `compose.yaml` say that on Docker Desktop you replace `network_mode` with `ports: ["127.0.0.1:37790:37790"]` and set `ALETHEIA_HOST=0.0.0.0`. A non-loopback bind turns on Hub login. Create an admin token first, as [Sync](../29-sync.md) describes.

The usual commands:

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose logs -f
docker compose down
```

One limit follows from how the hooks work. A hook or CLI command on your host opens the host's `hub.db` directly. It does not call the container. A container with its own `aletheia-data` volume therefore holds a different database from `~/.aletheia/hub.db`. To share one database you would have to mount the host data directory at `/data`. I did not test that, and the `aletheia` user in the container needs write access to the files.

## Next steps

- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) - port in use, an old dashboard after an upgrade, and a database that will not open.
- [Configuration reference](../reference/configuration.md) - every environment variable.
- [Model providers](model-providers.md) - put provider variables into the unit.
- [Operations notes](../07-operations.md) - the longer internal notes on running the server.

---

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/guides/model-providers.html

# Model providers: none, Claude CLI, OpenAI-compatible and Ollama


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) runs without any model. A model provider is optional, and it only changes how facts are extracted from your session summaries and notes. This page lists the providers, the environment variables, what leaves your machine, and what the measurements say.

## The default: no provider

With nothing set, `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER` is `none`. Extraction uses a rule extractor that makes no network call. It accepts a plain "subject verb object" sentence and skips everything else, so it is quiet rather than clever.

```bash
aletheia compress
```

```text
Extraction mode: rules; keyword only
queue: {"pending":0,"running":0,"done":1,"failed":0,"oldestPendingEpoch":null}
last: 1 memories, 1 window(s), 0 new fact(s), 0 rejected, 0 embedded
```

The measured limits, from the project README (retrieval numbers on LoCoMo, not answer accuracy):

- Facts from the rule extractor add about 0.4 points of Recall@5. The README text says 57.3% to 57.7%, while its table lists the raw-turns baseline as 57.4%. The README also reports that the dataset's own facts added 7.3 points. These are measured-by-us numbers.
- The first run with a small local model failed. Ollama `llama3.2:1b` answered a trivial chat call, but the fact-extraction prompt over a two-turn window returned HTTP 500 after 4 minutes 41 seconds, and no fact was stored. The raw note is in [provider-note.txt](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/bench/results/2026-10-26/provider-note.txt).
- No provider extraction recall number is published. Answer accuracy is not measured.

See [Benchmarks](../project/benchmarks.md) for the full table.

## What a provider is used for

I read the code for every place a provider is called.

| Use | Trigger | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Fact extraction | The server's background worker, and `aletheia compress` | A provider from `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER` or `ALETHEIA_PROVIDERS` |
| Compress events into observations | The **Compress now** button in Knowledge, Import and export | `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER` other than `none` |
| Work view refresh (goals, grouping, reviews, story) | The server, every 10 minutes, when `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER` is not `none` | The claude-mem database and `python3` |
| Plain-language card text ("human copy") | The server, when both `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_API_KEY` and `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_MODEL` are set | Those two variables. It ignores `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER`. |

Not model calls:

- Summaries. Session and project summaries are built from stored facts as a bullet list. I found no model call in that code.
- Reranking. The cross-encoder in `src/hub/rerank.mjs` is used by the benchmark script. I found no call to it from the CLI, the server or the MCP tools.
- Embeddings. They are a separate optional feature (see below).

If you want a provider for extraction only, turn the Work view refresh off. Without this, `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER=openai` on the server prints `refresh   : on (openai, every 10 min)`.

```bash
ALETHEIA_AUTO_REFRESH=false
```

## Providers and presets

`ALETHEIA_PROVIDER` takes one of these values. Anything else stops with `Unknown provider "<name>". Use one of: none, local, openai, openrouter, claude-cli, fake.` The value `fake` is for tests.

| Value | What it calls |
|---|---|
| `none` | Nothing. Rule extractor only. |
| `local` | An OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `ALETHEIA_LOCAL_BASE_URL`. The default is Ollama's `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions`. |
| `openai` | `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_BASE_URL`, default `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`, with `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_API_KEY`. |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions` with `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_API_KEY`. |
| `claude-cli` | The `claude` program in print mode. |

`ALETHEIA_PROVIDERS` takes an ordered list of presets: `ollama`, `lmstudio`, `llamacpp`, `local`, `openai`, `openrouter`, `claude-cli` and `anthropic-compatible`. `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER=ollama` is not valid; `ollama` is a preset name for the list only.

| Preset | URL |
|---|---|
| `ollama` | `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions` |
| `lmstudio` | `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/chat/completions` |
| `llamacpp` | `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions` |
| `local` | `ALETHEIA_LOCAL_BASE_URL` |
| `openai`, `openrouter` | The public endpoints above, API key required |
| `anthropic-compatible` | `ALETHEIA_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. There is no default, because Anthropic publishes no OpenAI-shaped chat endpoint. Point it at a gateway that has one. |

A selected provider that is incomplete stops with a message that names the setting:

```text
Provider "openai" needs a model: set ALETHEIA_OPENAI_MODEL or ALETHEIA_EXTRACT_MODEL.
Provider "ollama" needs a model: set ALETHEIA_OPENAI_MODEL or ALETHEIA_EXTRACT_MODEL.
Provider "anthropic-compatible" needs a URL: set ALETHEIA_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL.
```

The extraction worker in the server does not stop on a bad provider setting. It falls back to the rule extractor. The Work view refresh is different: with `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER=openai` and no model, `aletheia-server` printed the `needs a model` error and exited in my test. Set `ALETHEIA_AUTO_REFRESH=false` to avoid that path.

## Set one up

Local model with Ollama. Pull a model first with Ollama. The model name is yours to choose.

```bash
ALETHEIA_PROVIDER=local ALETHEIA_OPENAI_MODEL=llama3.2:1b aletheia compress
```

The variable `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_MODEL` names the model for every provider except `claude-cli`. Use `ALETHEIA_EXTRACT_MODEL` to name a different model for extraction.

OpenAI-compatible hosted API:

```bash
ALETHEIA_PROVIDER=openai \
ALETHEIA_OPENAI_API_KEY=<your key> \
ALETHEIA_OPENAI_MODEL=<model name> \
aletheia compress
```

Set `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_BASE_URL` to use another OpenAI-style endpoint with the `openai` value.

Claude CLI:

```bash
ALETHEIA_PROVIDER=claude-cli aletheia compress
```

The code runs `claude -p --output-format json --no-session-persistence --tools "" --setting-sources ""` and sends the prompt on standard input. It uses `haiku` for extraction and `sonnet` for summaries unless you set `ALETHEIA_EXTRACT_MODEL` or `ALETHEIA_SUMMARY_MODEL`. `ALETHEIA_CLAUDE_BIN` names the program. I did not run this provider for this page.

For the server, set the same variables in the environment of the process. For a systemd service that means `Environment=` lines. See [Run as a service](run-as-a-service.md).

Version 0.1.10 showed provider fields on the Settings page, but no code read the saved values, so they were removed. Use environment variables.

## Fallback chain

`ALETHEIA_PROVIDERS=ollama,openai` tries the providers in order.

- A quota error, HTTP 408, 425, 429 or 5xx, or a timeout moves the call to the next provider. The failed provider rests for `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER_COOLDOWN_MS` (60,000 by default).
- An error the service can answer, such as a 400, is raised. It is not hidden by a fallback.
- At most `ALETHEIA_MAX_CONCURRENT` requests run at once (1 by default).
- `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS` (60,000 by default) applies to the chain only. A single provider uses a 5 minute timeout.
- A failed extraction job retries with backoff, up to 5 attempts. After that it is marked failed, and `aletheia doctor` shows it in the `queue` row.

One display quirk: with only `ALETHEIA_PROVIDERS` set, the server banner prints `extraction: worker on (rule-based)` and `aletheia compress` prints `Extraction mode: none`. Both read `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER`. The chain is still used for the calls.

## Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER` | `none` | One provider, see above. |
| `ALETHEIA_PROVIDERS` | empty | Ordered chain of presets. Wins over `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER` when set. |
| `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_API_KEY` | empty | Key for `openai`, `openrouter` and the presets with a key. |
| `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_MODEL` | empty | Model for extraction. |
| `ALETHEIA_OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` | Endpoint for `openai`. The README table lists an OpenRouter URL as the default; the code uses the OpenAI URL. |
| `ALETHEIA_LOCAL_BASE_URL` | Ollama URL | Endpoint for `local`. |
| `ALETHEIA_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | empty | Gateway for `anthropic-compatible`. |
| `ALETHEIA_EXTRACT_MODEL`, `ALETHEIA_SUMMARY_MODEL` | empty | Per-stage model names. |
| `ALETHEIA_CLAUDE_BIN` | `claude` | The Claude CLI program. |
| `ALETHEIA_FACT_MAX_EPISODES` | 20 | Episodes per request. |
| `ALETHEIA_FACT_CHAR_BUDGET` | 12000 | Characters per request. |
| `ALETHEIA_PRICE_IN_PER_1K`, `ALETHEIA_PRICE_OUT_PER_1K` | 0 | Your own prices, for the cost estimate. |
| `ALETHEIA_MODE` | `code` | Extraction style: `code`, `chill`, `language-en` or `language-es`. |
| `ALETHEIA_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE` | empty | Output language, see below. |
| `ALETHEIA_AUTO_REFRESH` | on | `false` turns the Work view refresh off. |

## What is sent to the model

I started a local mock endpoint, pointed `ALETHEIA_PROVIDER=local` at it, queued one job and recorded the request body. A hosted provider receives the same body.

The request has the keys `model`, `stream`, `temperature` and `messages`. The message holds:

- the fixed extraction instructions, the mode line and the language line;
- the project name and the episode ids;
- one log line per source: id, timestamp, tool name, kind and the text.

The sources are session summaries (the last assistant message that the Stop hook captured) and saved notes. Prompts and tool events are not fact sources, so they are not sent by this path.

The text is redacted again right before the call. In the test, a summary imported from claude-mem held a fake AWS key id, and the request carried `[redacted:aws-key-id]`. The `Authorization` header was absent because no key was set. Facts that come back are redacted again before storing.

What the redaction does not cover:

- The Compress now route sends the title and the first 400 characters of the text of event rows, and only the title of prompt rows. They were redacted when captured, and that route does not redact again.
- I found no call to the redaction function in the Work view refresh code or in the human copy code.
- Redaction is pattern-based and cannot be complete. See [Privacy and redaction](../concepts/privacy.md).

## Cost and privacy notes

- A local provider keeps the text on your machine. A hosted provider receives the redacted text above, under that provider's terms. `claude-cli` sends it through your Claude login.
- Aletheia records an estimate for every call: tokens are characters divided by 4, not the vendor's count. Prices default to 0, because this project does not guess a vendor price. Set the two price variables to get a cost estimate.
- Each request is bounded by the episode and character budgets above, and each episode is cut to 2,000 characters.
- Extraction runs after sessions end, not inside a hook. Hooks never call a model.
- The rule extractor makes no network call.

### Embeddings are separate

Semantic search and fact vectors use an optional package, `@huggingface/transformers`. They need no provider. They run from `aletheia embed` and `aletheia search --semantic` (which you start on purpose) and, only if you set `ALETHEIA_EMBED_FACTS=1`, from `aletheia compress`. The first use downloads a model, about 35 MB according to the code comment, into `~/.aletheia/models`. Without the package installed, none of this runs. `aletheia compress` creates no embeddings by default, so it makes no download.

## Output language

`ALETHEIA_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE` and `aletheia language` set the language of extracted facts. The setting adds one line to the model prompt. It has no effect on the rule extractor, which does not translate.

```bash
aletheia language set es --project shop
aletheia language set pt_BR
aletheia language
aletheia language set "" --project shop
```

```text
Output language for shop: es
Output language for default: pt-br
shop                     es
default                  pt-br
Cleared the output language for shop; it follows the extraction mode.
```

A language tag is checked when you set it. Use a BCP 47 tag such as `en`, `es` or `pt-BR`. The tag is stored in lower case. A bad tag stops with `"<text>" is not a language tag.`

The order of precedence is: the project's saved language, then the saved `default` language, then `ALETHEIA_OUTPUT_LANGUAGE`, then the extraction mode. An empty value clears a saved language. The prompt keeps code, paths, names and identifiers unchanged.

## Next steps

- [Facts and contradictions](../33-facts.md) - the quality gate that every extracted fact passes.
- [Privacy and redaction](../concepts/privacy.md) - what is redacted, and when.
- [Configuration reference](../reference/configuration.md) - every environment variable.
- [Benchmarks](../project/benchmarks.md) - the retrieval numbers behind the default.
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) - failed jobs and doctor output.

# Troubleshooting Aletheia: port in use, MCP closed, no memories and more


This page lists problems people hit with Aletheia (aletheia-mem) and the exact command that fixes each one. Every fix was checked against the code, and most were reproduced in a temporary home folder with a temporary data directory.

Start with `aletheia doctor`. It checks the host and port, the server, the hook entries, the spool, file permissions, the last capture, the job queue and the database.

## Port 37790 is already in use (EADDRINUSE)

Cause: another process holds the port. The usual one is the service you already started, or a second `aletheia-server`.

```text
error: Failed to start server. Is port 37999 in use?
 syscall: "listen",
   errno: 0,
    code: "EADDRINUSE"
```

The number in the message is the port you configured. Fix: find the owner, or use another port.

```bash
ss -ltnp | grep 37790
systemctl --user status aletheia
ALETHEIA_PORT=37791 aletheia-server
```

On macOS use `lsof -nP -iTCP:37790 -sTCP:LISTEN` instead of `ss` (not tested on a Mac). If you run a service, change its port with `ALETHEIA_PORT=37791 aletheia service install --write`. See [Run as a service](run-as-a-service.md).

## `aletheia-server --help` started the server

Cause: the server binary has no help flag. It reads only `--host` and `--behind-tls`, ignores anything else and starts. I ran it with `--help` on a test port and it printed:

```text
aletheia-mem listening on http://localhost:38417
  source db : ~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db (read-only)
  data dir  : ~/.aletheia
  refresh   : off (set ALETHEIA_PROVIDER=claude-cli|openai to enable)
  extraction: worker on (rule-based)
```

Fix: press Ctrl-C. For command help, run `aletheia` with no arguments. It prints the full command list. Settings are environment variables; see the [Configuration reference](../reference/configuration.md).

## Claude Code shows the aletheia MCP server as CONNECTION_CLOSED

Cause: the entry in `~/.claude.json` holds the absolute path of Bun and of `mcp.mjs`. If that path no longer exists, the process cannot start and Claude Code reports the connection as closed. This happens after the package moves, for example when you switch Node versions or the npm prefix. In a test I pointed the entry at a missing path and started it by hand:

```text
error: Module not found "/old/node/lib/node_modules/aletheia-mem/bin/mcp.mjs"
```

Fix: write the entry again. The installer replaces the `aletheia` entry with the current paths.

```bash
aletheia install claude-code --verify
aletheia install claude-code --write
```

The first command printed `drift  mcp` for the broken entry. The second wrote only `~/.claude.json` and left the hooks as they were. Start a new Claude Code session afterwards. `aletheia connect claude-code` is not the fix: for Claude Code it prints a `claude mcp add` command instead of editing the file.

To check an entry by hand, read the `command` and `args` under `mcpServers.aletheia` in `~/.claude.json` and confirm both files exist. The MCP server was listed by the real Claude Code 2.1.312 CLI on 2026-10-27.

## The dashboard looks old after an upgrade

Three causes, in the order to check them.

1. The installed package is older than you think. More than one install can be on the path.

   ```bash
   aletheia --version
   npm ls -g aletheia-mem
   which -a aletheia
   ```

2. The running server still has the old code. The server reads `index.html` once and keeps it in memory, so a running server serves the old page until it restarts.

   ```bash
   systemctl --user restart aletheia
   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:37790/v1/info
   ```

   The `/v1/info` answer includes `"version"`, the version of the code the server runs. If you set `ALETHEIA_API_KEY`, send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

3. The browser kept old files. The page itself is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The JavaScript and CSS files under `/work-view/` carry no cache header, so a browser can reuse an old copy. Hard reload the page (Ctrl+Shift+R, or Cmd+Shift+R on macOS).

After an upgrade, also run `aletheia install <tool> --write` for each tool, so the hook bundle in the data directory is rebuilt.

## `npm install -g aletheia-mem@X` returns E404 right after a release

Cause: the registry does not list that version yet. I could not observe a release delay, but a version the registry does not have gives the same message:

```text
npm error code E404
npm error 404 No match found for version 0.1.999
```

Fix: ask the registry what it has, then wait and retry.

```bash
npm view aletheia-mem version
npm view aletheia-mem@0.1.10 version
npm install -g aletheia-mem@latest
```

If `npm view` does not show the new version, wait a few minutes. `@latest` installs whatever the registry shows as the newest.

## Hooks are installed but no memories appear

Work through these checks in order.

1. Read the doctor rows.

   ```bash
   aletheia doctor | grep -E "hooks|spool|last capture|server"
   ```

   `hooks claude-code  5/5` means the five hook entries are in the settings file. It does not mean a hook ran. `last capture` shows the time of the newest stored prompt, event or summary. `no capture yet` means nothing has been stored.

2. Run a hook by hand. It should store one memory and exit 0.

   ```bash
   echo '{"hook_event_name":"UserPromptSubmit","session_id":"s-1","cwd":"/tmp/demo","prompt":"Add a health endpoint"}' | aletheia hook claude-code UserPromptSubmit
   aletheia search health
   ```

   ```text
   #1 2026-10-29 [note] Add a health endpoint (demo, claude-code)
   ```

3. Look at the spool. When the database cannot be opened, a hook writes the item to `<data dir>/spool/hook-spool.jsonl` and the next successful hook replays it. In a test with a broken database path the doctor row read `FAIL spool  1 item(s) at .../spool/hook-spool.jsonl`, and the next good hook emptied it. A spool that stays full points at a database problem; see the sections below.

4. Check that the host and your shell use the same data directory. A hook reads `ALETHEIA_DATA_DIR` from the environment of the tool that starts it. If you set it only in your shell, the hook and the dashboard use different databases.

5. Check excluded projects. A project named in `ALETHEIA_EXCLUDED_PROJECTS` is skipped before any row is written, and the hook still exits 0. Only the environment variable is read; the Settings page no longer has an excluded-projects field.

6. Check what the tool can send. Command Code has no prompt hook and no session-end hook, so prompts are not captured there. `SessionStart` only injects context and stores no row.

7. Codex: Codex requires non-managed hooks to be reviewed and trusted before they run. Its documentation says new or changed hooks are marked for review and skipped until trusted, and that you inspect and trust them with `/hooks` in the CLI (https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks, fetched 2026-10-29). I did not test whether a reinstall that changes the hook command asks for a new review.

8. Other tools. Cursor, Gemini CLI and Windsurf: config written from docs, not tested on a real install. No hook ran in Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf or OpenCode. OpenCode has MCP and rules only.

Hooks ran in real sessions of Claude Code (two days of use), Command Code (one short session) and Codex CLI (one interactive session), one user on one machine.

Facts are separate from memories. A memory appears as soon as a hook stores it. Facts need extraction, which the server worker or `aletheia compress` runs after a session ends.

## The rules page is empty

Cause: rules live in the Aletheia database. They are not read from `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` or any other tool file. A new install has no rules, and `aletheia install` writes an empty block (`0 rules`).

Fix: add rules, or import them from a file you already have.

```bash
aletheia rules list
aletheia rules import --tool claude-code --global
aletheia rules import --tool claude-code --dir /path/to/project
```

In the dashboard use Rules, then **Import**. Details are in [Write rules once](write-rules-once.md).

## The session-start block is too large

Cause: the block that a hook injects is capped at 6,000 characters. It holds pinned memories (up to 50), the 20 newest memories, up to 5 recent session requests, up to 10 facts and every enabled rule. The code cuts the text at the end, and the rules come near the end, so a large block can cut off rules first.

Fix: measure it, then shrink it.

```bash
aletheia context --project shop | wc -c
```

- Unpin memories you no longer need, in the Knowledge tab.
- Hide a memory: `aletheia dismiss <id>`. Undo with `aletheia restore <id>`.
- Retire a rule you do not need: `aletheia rules retire <id>`.
- Set **Facts in context** to `off` in Connections, then Settings. The default `auto` already hides low-confidence rule-extracted facts.

The Connections page **What tools receive** shows what a tool gets. See [Session-start context](../concepts/session-context.md).

## Facts look like noise

Cause: the extractor stored sentences that read like narration or code. A quality gate now checks new facts. Older rows can still fail it.

Fix: dry run first. The command is a dry run until you add `--apply`.

```bash
aletheia facts clean
aletheia facts clean --apply
aletheia restore fact:42
```

```text
Dry run: 0 of 0 fact(s) fail the quality gate.
Add --apply to dismiss the failures (reversible with aletheia restore fact:<id>).
```

On a store with failing facts the command prints a count per reason and up to 10 examples for each. The `--dry-run` flag is not read; leaving `--apply` off is the dry run. The gate rules are in [Facts and contradictions](../33-facts.md).

## Database is locked or busy

Cause: SQLite allows one writer at a time. Another process holds a write lock for longer than Aletheia waits. The store waits 3 seconds. I held a write transaction open from another process and ran `aletheia save`:

```text
SQLiteError: database is locked
```

The call returned after about 3 seconds. Once its store is open, a hook lowers the wait to 50 milliseconds and spools the item instead of failing the session.

Fix: find and end the process that holds the lock. Common ones are a long import, a backup tool, or a `sqlite3` shell with an open transaction. Do not put the data directory on a network drive. SQLite's documentation says WAL mode does not work over a network filesystem and allows one writer at a time (https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html, fetched 2026-10-29). Run `aletheia doctor` afterwards. The spool row shows whether hooks were waiting.

## `/healthz` returns 503, or doctor shows `FAIL database`

Cause: the database or search-index check failed. There are two very different reasons.

**A false alarm while something writes.** Before this change, `quick_check` could print `fts5: corruption found reading blob ...` for a healthy index while a hook or sync wrote at the same moment. On the author's service it appeared in about 1 of 40 `/healthz` calls; a snapshot copy of the same database passed `quick_check` and the FTS integrity check, and real search queries never failed (0 errors in 400,000 queries during the test). The health check now retries three times, and if only search-index rows still complain it runs a real search query. When that works it reports `quick_check ok (FTS integrity check skipped while writes were in progress; FTS query answered)`. If your version is older, upgrade.

**A damaged index.** I reproduced this error by damaging a search-index block in a copy of a test database. It stays after the retries and a real search query fails too:

```text
FAIL database             fts5: corruption found reading blob 687194767361 from table "memories_fts"
```

`aletheia optimize` fails on such an index with the same message. I do not know what damages an index on a real machine.

Fix: back up first. Stop the server and copy `hub.db`, `hub.db-wal` and `hub.db-shm` together; see [Backup, export and import](backup-export-import.md). Then rebuild the two search indexes from the stored rows. The `sqlite3` shell often lacks FTS5, so use Bun:

```bash
cat > rebuild-fts.mjs <<'EOF'
import { Database } from "bun:sqlite";
const db = new Database(process.argv[2]);
db.exec("INSERT INTO memories_fts(memories_fts) VALUES('rebuild')");
db.exec("INSERT INTO facts_fts(facts_fts) VALUES('rebuild')");
db.close();
EOF
bun rebuild-fts.mjs ~/.aletheia/hub.db
aletheia doctor | grep -E "database|fts"
```

SQLite documents the `rebuild` command as rebuilding an index from the content table (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html, fetched 2026-10-29). In my test, `database` went from FAIL to `quick_check ok` after the rebuild. If `quick_check` still fails, restore from a backup or from an export bundle.

## doctor shows `FAIL server`

Cause: the server is not running, or it listens on a port other than the one doctor checks. Doctor reads `ALETHEIA_PORT` from your shell. Hooks and the CLI do not need the server, so this row alone is not a capture problem.

Fix: start the server or the service, or set the port.

```bash
ALETHEIA_PORT=37791 aletheia doctor
```

An `HTTP 503` detail means the server answered and its health check failed; see the section above.

## A line says `mode 0644 -> 0600`

```text
aletheia: file ~/.aletheia/hub.db mode 0644 -> 0600
```

Cause: Aletheia tightens the data directory to `0700` and the database files to `0600` when it opens them, and prints one line when it changes a mode. It is a notice, not an error. `aletheia doctor` has a `permissions` row that reports loose modes.

## Windows notes

- Continuous integration runs the test suite on Windows (GitHub's `windows-latest` runner, Bun 1.3.10). Two hook checks (Windsurf and Gemini CLI) and one temp-folder cleanup check are skipped there. No real tool was tried on Windows. Treat Windows as tested in CI only.
- `aletheia service install` writes nothing on Windows. Start `aletheia-server` yourself or use Task Scheduler.
- `aletheia doctor` skips the permissions check on Windows, because there are no POSIX mode bits.
- The CLI runs on Bun, not Node. Install Bun 1.1 or newer.

## Collect a useful bug report

Open an issue at https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/issues and choose the Bug report template. Collect this first:

```bash
aletheia --version
bun --version
uname -a
aletheia doctor | sed "s#$HOME#~#g"
aletheia install --list
```

- Add the host tool and its version, for example `claude --version`.
- Add the exact command, what you expected and what happened, with the error text.
- `aletheia doctor --json` gives the same checks as JSON.
- Replace your home folder with `~`, as the `sed` above does. Doctor output holds file paths and your user name. It is built not to include API keys, but read it before you paste it.
- Do not paste `~/.claude.json`, a settings file or an environment dump without removing tokens. Remove prompts and `<private>` content.
- For a security problem, do not open a public issue. Use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting on the repository (Security tab), as `SECURITY.md` describes.

## Next steps

- [Run as a service](run-as-a-service.md) - ports, logs and restarts for the server.
- [Backup, export and import](backup-export-import.md) - copy the database files safely before a repair.
- [Tools overview](../tools/overview.md) - what was checked on a real install, per tool.
- [Reference: hooks](../reference/hooks.md) - the events each hook handles.
