Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/reference/hooks.html

# Aletheia hooks reference: events, payloads, redaction and fail-open behavior


In Aletheia (aletheia-mem), a hook is a command that a host, the AI coding tool, runs at a session event. The command is `aletheia hook <tool> <event>`. It reads one JSON payload on stdin, stores a redacted memory, and never blocks the host.

The examples on this page were run on 2026-10-29 against version 0.1.10 in a temporary home and data directory. Paths are shortened with `...`. The payloads are written by hand from the fields each adapter reads. The repository holds no recorded payload files; its tests write payloads inline.

## What a hook does

`aletheia hook claude-code PostToolUse` does these steps, in order. Source: [src/hub/hooks/run.mjs](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/hooks/run.mjs).

1. Read stdin. Empty or broken JSON becomes an empty payload.
2. Pick the adapter for the host. An unknown host name returns at once.
3. Work out the project from the payload's working directory, without starting `git`.
4. Skip the item if the project is in `ALETHEIA_EXCLUDED_PROJECTS`. Nothing is written.
5. Build the memory from the payload and redact it. This step touches no database.
6. Open `hub.db` with a 50 ms busy timeout, drain the spool, then store the memory, queue compression or mark the session ended.
7. For a session-start event only, print the context block on stdout.
8. Exit 0.

A hook makes no network call and no model call. Compression only queues a job. A worker started by `aletheia-server` or `aletheia compress` runs it later.

## Verification status

- MCP server listed by the real CLI on 2026-10-27: Claude Code 2.1.312, Command Code 1.88.1, Codex 0.130.0, OpenCode 1.18.33.
- Hooks ran in real sessions of Claude Code (two days of use), Command Code (one short session) and Codex CLI (one interactive session), one user on one machine.
- Cursor, Gemini CLI and Windsurf: "config written from docs, not tested on a real install". No hook ran in Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf or OpenCode.

Payload field names are the ones the adapter source cites, from host documentation the project author fetched on 2026-10-26. I did not fetch any host documentation on 2026-10-29. **UNVERIFIED:** that Cursor, Gemini CLI and Windsurf send exactly these fields, because no hook ran in them. A real hook run or a fresh read of each host's hooks page would verify it. See [Tools overview](../tools/overview.md).

## Events per host

`aletheia install --list` prints the events each installer wires (the note lines are left out):

```
tool          capability   verification     detected  events
claude-code   full         mcp-verified      no        SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd
command-code  full         mcp-verified      no        SessionStart, PostToolUse, Stop
cursor        full         from-docs-only    no        sessionStart, beforeSubmitPrompt, postToolUse, afterAgentResponse, stop, sessionEnd
codex         full         mcp-verified      no        SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd
gemini-cli    full         from-docs-only    no        SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterTool, AfterAgent, SessionEnd
windsurf      full         from-docs-only    no        pre_user_prompt, post_run_command, post_write_code, post_cascade_response
opencode      mcp+rules    mcp-verified      no        none
```

In this column `mcp-verified` means only the line about the real CLI listing the MCP server above. `from-docs-only` means config written from docs, not tested on a real install. `detected` is `no` here because the temporary home has no tool folders.

OpenCode and Claude Desktop have no hooks. For OpenCode the installer writes the MCP entry and the rules block only. Claude Desktop has an MCP entry only; see [Claude Desktop](../claude-desktop.md).

## What each event captures

Every row is from the adapter in `src/hub/hooks/`. "Summary" is a memory of kind `summary`; "queues compression" adds a job for the extraction worker; "ends the session" records a session-end row.

| Host | Event | What Aletheia does | Payload fields read |
|---|---|---|---|
| claude-code | SessionStart | Prints context. Prints nothing when `source` is `resume`. | `source` |
| claude-code | UserPromptSubmit | Stores the prompt. | `prompt` |
| claude-code | PostToolUse | Stores a tool event. | `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_response` |
| claude-code | Stop, SessionEnd | Stores a summary, queues compression, ends the session. | `last_assistant_message` |
| command-code | SessionStart | Prints context. Nothing on `resume`. | `source` |
| command-code | PostToolUse | Stores a tool event. | `tool_name`, `tool_display_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_response` |
| command-code | Stop | Queues compression, ends the session. Stores no memory. | none |
| codex | SessionStart | Prints context. Nothing on `resume`. | `source` |
| codex | UserPromptSubmit | Stores the prompt. | `prompt` |
| codex | PostToolUse | Stores a tool event. | `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_response` |
| codex | Stop | Stores a summary, queues compression, ends the session. | `last_assistant_message` |
| codex | SessionEnd | Queues compression, ends the session. No memory. | none |
| cursor | sessionStart | Prints context as `{"additional_context": ...}`. | `workspace_roots` |
| cursor | beforeSubmitPrompt | Stores the prompt. | `prompt` |
| cursor | postToolUse | Stores a tool event. | `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_output` |
| cursor | afterAgentResponse | Stores a summary. | `text` |
| cursor | stop, sessionEnd | Queues compression, ends the session. | none |
| gemini-cli | SessionStart | Prints context. Nothing on `resume`. | `source` |
| gemini-cli | BeforeAgent | Stores the prompt. | `prompt` |
| gemini-cli | AfterTool | Stores a tool event. | `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `tool_response` |
| gemini-cli | AfterAgent | Stores a summary, queues compression. | `prompt_response` |
| gemini-cli | SessionEnd | Queues compression, ends the session. | none |
| windsurf | pre_user_prompt | Stores the prompt. | `tool_info.user_prompt` |
| windsurf | post_run_command | Stores a `Shell` event. | `tool_info.command_line` |
| windsurf | post_write_code | Stores a `Write` event. | `tool_info.file_path`, `tool_info.edits` |
| windsurf | post_cascade_response | Stores a summary, queues compression. | `tool_info.response` |

Command Code has no `UserPromptSubmit` or `SessionEnd` hook, so prompts and end-of-session summaries are not captured there. Windsurf has no session-start event, so it receives no context. Cursor's `stop` payload carries no assistant text, so `afterAgentResponse` stores the summary.

Shared fields:

- Project: `cwd`. Cursor uses `workspace_roots[0]`, then `cwd`. Windsurf uses `tool_info.cwd`, then `cwd`. With no directory the project is `default`. The key is the repository folder name found by walking up to `.git`.
- Session id: `session_id` (also `sessionId` for Claude Code and Command Code). Cursor uses `conversation_id` as a fallback. Windsurf uses `trajectory_id`.
- Event name: the second argument. If it is missing, `hook_event_name` or `event` from the payload is used. Names are matched without regard to case.

## The hook command and its timeouts

`aletheia install <tool> --write` adds this command to the host's config. The trailing comment is the marker the uninstaller looks for:

```
.../.bun/bin/bun .../data/aletheia.bundle.mjs hook claude-code PostToolUse # aletheia-managed
```

The installer builds `aletheia.bundle.mjs` in the data directory so a hook loads one file, not a dozen. If the build fails it falls back to the source CLI. The `timeout` the installer writes into each host's config:

| Host | `timeout` written | Matcher written |
|---|---|---|
| claude-code | 10 | SessionStart `startup\|clear\|compact`; PostToolUse `*` |
| command-code | 10 | none |
| codex | 10, SessionEnd 3 | SessionStart `startup\|clear\|compact\|fork` |
| cursor | 10 | none |
| gemini-cli | 10000 | none |
| windsurf | none | none |

The code notes that Gemini CLI counts milliseconds. **UNVERIFIED:** the unit the other hosts use for their `timeout` (seconds is likely). Verify it in each host's hooks documentation.

Aletheia also has its own limit. `bin/aletheia.mjs` starts a 150 ms watchdog and exits 0 when it fires. A `PostToolUse` hook took 0.04 to 0.05 s on a small database. One that waited on a held write lock took about 0.1 s.

## Fail-open behavior

A hook prints nothing on stdout and exits 0 on every error. A broken hook never stops a session.

```
$ echo '{}' | aletheia hook nosuch Foo          # unknown host: no output, exit 0
$ echo 'not json' | aletheia hook claude-code PostToolUse   # exit 0
$ aletheia hook claude-code Stop < /dev/null    # exit 0
```

- **Excluded project.** With `ALETHEIA_EXCLUDED_PROJECTS=shop` a prompt in project `shop` printed nothing, and no row exists for its session.
- **Nothing to store.** A skipped tool (`TodoWrite`, `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `ToolSearch`, `todo_write`) or an empty prompt leaves the database unopened.
- **Store busy or unavailable.** The already redacted item goes to `<data>/spool/hook-spool.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, mode `0600`.
- **The spool drains.** The next hook that opens the store replays the spool first. The live file is renamed before the replay, so a parallel hook's append is not lost. Items that still fail are written back.
- **Watchdog.** If the 150 ms watchdog fires, the process exits 0 at once. Reading the code, an item still in flight at that moment is not spooled. I did not trigger this case.
- **Stderr.** One-line permission repairs, such as `aletheia: data directory ... mode 0775 -> 0700`, go to stderr, not stdout.

A real run with `hub.db` replaced by a directory, then repaired:

```
$ echo '{"hook_event_name":"PostToolUse","cwd":".../shop","session_id":"demo-3","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"ls -la"},"tool_response":"ok"}' | aletheia hook claude-code PostToolUse
$ cat .../data2/spool/hook-spool.jsonl
{"kind":"memory","memory":{"project":"shop","tool":"claude-code","sessionId":"demo-3","kind":"event","type":"event","title":"Bash: ls -la","narrative":"input: {\"command\":\"ls -la\"}\n\noutput: ok"},"at":1793303306263}
$ aletheia doctor | grep spool
FAIL spool                1 item(s) at .../data2/spool/hook-spool.jsonl
$ rmdir .../data2/hub.db
$ echo '{... "command":"pwd" ...}' | aletheia hook claude-code PostToolUse
$ aletheia search "ls -la" --project shop
#1 2026-10-29 [event] Bash: ls -la (shop, claude-code)
$ aletheia doctor | grep spool
ok   spool                empty
```

A second run held the write lock from another process with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The hook spooled its item, and the next hook stored both.

## Redaction and limits

The adapter redacts each field before it is spooled or stored. `<private>...</private>` blocks become `[private]`. Patterns replace API keys (Anthropic, OpenAI-style, Stripe), GitHub, GitLab, npm and Slack tokens, JWTs, AWS key ids, Google keys, private key blocks, bearer headers, passwords in URLs, and `password`, `secret`, `token` or `api_key` assignments. The list is in [src/hub/redact.mjs](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/redact.mjs). See [Privacy and redaction](../concepts/privacy.md).

```
$ echo '{"hook_event_name":"UserPromptSubmit","cwd":".../shop","session_id":"p1","prompt":"Rotate the key <private>hunter2-very-secret</private> before Friday, token=abcd1234efgh"}' | aletheia hook claude-code UserPromptSubmit
$ aletheia search "Rotate the key"
#20 2026-10-29 [note] Rotate the key [private] before Friday, token=[redacted] (shop, claude-code)
```

Stored sizes: a prompt keeps 8000 characters, a tool event 1500 (`input:` then `output:`), a summary 4000. Titles are cut to 120, 160 and 140 characters.

## Test a hook by hand

Pipe a payload into the command the installer wrote, or into `aletheia hook` directly. Use a temporary data directory so your own memory stays untouched.

```
$ export ALETHEIA_DATA_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
$ echo '{"hook_event_name":"SessionStart","cwd":".../shop","session_id":"demo-1","source":"startup"}' | aletheia hook claude-code SessionStart
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"<aletheia-memory>\nRecalled memory from earlier sessions. ... # Memory for shop\n\n## Pinned\n- #1 19:46 [D] Use pnpm, not npm, in the shop repo ... </aletheia-memory>"}}
$ echo '{"hook_event_name":"Stop","cwd":".../shop","session_id":"demo-1","last_assistant_message":"Fixed the failing test and switched the repo to pnpm."}' | aletheia hook claude-code Stop
$ aletheia search "failing test" --project shop
#5 2026-10-29 [summary] Session summary: Fixed the failing test and switched the repo to pnpm. (shop, claude-code)
```

The same check ran for Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Command Code and Codex with hand-written payloads, and each stored the expected row. That tests the adapter code. It does not show that those hosts send these fields. Payload shapes for every host are in [test/e2e-more-hosts.test.mjs](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/test/e2e-more-hosts.test.mjs).

To check a whole session in a data directory, run `bun scripts/hook-check.mjs <data-dir> --tool claude-code` from a source checkout. It reads `hub.db` without writing, scans for secrets that escaped redaction, and prints PASS or FAIL per event. It supports `claude-code`, `codex` and `command-code`.

## Check hooks with aletheia doctor

`aletheia doctor` reads the host config files and counts the expected hook commands in each. It does not run a hook. A tool that is not installed is not a failure. A present config with missing hooks is.

```
$ aletheia doctor
ok   host                 127.0.0.1 (loopback)
ok   port                 37913
FAIL server               not reachable at http://127.0.0.1:37913/healthz
ok   hooks claude-code    5/5 in .../home/.claude/settings.json
ok   hooks cursor         6/6 in .../home/.cursor/hooks.json
ok   tool opencode        mcp+rules; no hook system shipped
ok   verify cursor        verified: verified 2026-10-26 — Cursor docs fetched 2026-10-26; Cursor is not installed on this machine
ok   spool                empty
ok   permissions          data dir 0700, db 0600
ok   last capture         no capture yet
ok   queue                0 pending, 0 running, 0 failed
```

- `server` calls `/healthz` on `ALETHEIA_PORT`. It fails when the server is not running, which does not stop hooks from working.
- `verify <tool>` says `verified` when a verification date is recorded and is under 180 days old. It is not proof that a real tool ran a hook. Read the text after the dash for what was checked.
- `spool` fails when items wait. `permissions`, `database`, `fts`, `queue` and `last capture` report the store. `--json` prints the checks as JSON.
- The exit status is 1 when any line is `FAIL`.

## Verify, uninstall and the manifest

`aletheia install <tool> --write` records each file it changed, with a SHA-256 hash and a backup name, in `<data>/install-manifest.json`. Every changed file also gets a copy named `<file>.aletheia-bak-<time>`.

```
$ aletheia install codex --verify
  ok        mcp      .../home/.codex/config.toml
  drift     hooks    .../home/.codex/hooks.json
  ok        rules    .../home/.codex/AGENTS.md
codex: drifted from the recorded install
```

`--verify` never writes. It exits 1 when a tool is not installed, or when any file is `missing`, `drift` or `unreadable`. With no tool name it checks every tool in the manifest.

`aletheia uninstall <tool>` is a dry run until `--write`. It removes the MCP entry, the hook entries marked `aletheia-managed` and the managed rules block, and keeps every other entry in each file.

```
$ aletheia uninstall codex --write
Codex CLI (codex)
  remove mcp      .../home/.codex/config.toml
  BLOCK  hooks    .../home/.codex/hooks.json  (file changed since install; rerun with --force)
  remove rules    .../home/.codex/AGENTS.md
Refused: a file changed after install. Review it, then rerun with --force to remove our entries anyway.
```

Two behaviors of 0.1.10 to know. First, when one file has drifted, the command exits 1 and prints `Refused`, but it has already cleaned the other files: the MCP entry and the rules block were gone afterward, and only the hooks file kept its entries. Second, before this fix the hooks line of an uninstall could carry the note `(no aletheia hooks)` even when the line said `remove`; the entries were removed. It now shows the note only when there is nothing to remove.

## Next steps

- [CLI reference](cli.md) - `hook`, `install`, `uninstall` and `doctor` with their flags.
- [Configuration](configuration.md) - the data directory, the spool path and `ALETHEIA_EXCLUDED_PROJECTS`.
- [Installer reference](../25-installers.md) - what each installer writes and the sources it used.
- [Troubleshooting](../guides/troubleshooting.md) - when a hook does not seem to run.

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/03-http-api.html

# 3. HTTP API

Base: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. All JSON responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store`. Pages carry
`Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.

## 3.1 Guards

| Guard | Applies to | Rule | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| **local only** | every `/api/*` route except `/health` | peer address is `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or `::ffff:127.0.0.1`; `Host` header names `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `::1`; none of `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Host`, `X-Real-IP` present | `403 {"error":"Work view is available only on this computer."}` |
| **same-origin JSON** | every POST | `Sec-Fetch-Site` is not `cross-site`; `Origin` is absent or exactly this server's loopback origin (same port); `Content-Type` is `application/json` | `403 {"error":"Review changes must come from the local work viewer."}` |
| **file origin** | `GET /api/work-view/file/...` | not cross-site, not cross-origin | `403 {"error":"Recorded files open only from the local work viewer."}` |

The server also binds to `127.0.0.1` only. The Host check defeats DNS rebinding; the Origin check defeats a
web page POSTing to your local port.

Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`. Validation errors are `400 {"error":"Invalid request body.","details":[{path,message}]}`.
An unknown route is `404` with an HTML `Cannot <METHOD> <path>` body, like Express.

## 3.2 Routes

### Static
| Route | Response |
|---|---|
| `GET /`, `/index.html` | the SPA shell (`public/index.html`) |
| `GET /work-view/*` | files from `public/` (`/work-view/assets/...`, `/work-view/favicon.png`) |
| `GET /health` | `{"status":"ok","timestamp":<ms>}` |

### `GET /api/work-view` — the snapshot
Returns the whole page state. Top-level fields, in order:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `1` | |
| `generatedAt` | ISO string | |
| `currentProject`, `currentProjectScope` | `""`, `[]` | Always empty in this design (no "current project" concept). |
| `agents` | `Agent[]` | Sessions and subagents with their work and recent activity. |
| `recentActivity` | `Activity[]` (<=160) | Newest first, each with `agentGroupId`. |
| `goals` | `Goals \| null` | Current goals; gains `alignedAt`. |
| `goalHistory` | `Goals[]` | Past months, newest first. |
| `rules`, `ruleScopes`, `rulesLearning` | | My Rules. |
| `humanRequests` | `Request[]` | One card per human request, newest first. |
| `unlinkedWork` | `Item[]` | Work items that could not be tied to a human request, each with `reason`. |
| `coverage` | object | Counts and limits (`workRows`, `workLimit`, `linkedWork`, `ownerWork`, `unattributedWork`, `observations`, `observationLimit`, `summaries`, `livePresenceAvailable:false`, `summaryMethod`, `fullHistoryUrl:"/viewer"`). |
| `revision` | string | `"<agentRevision>:<reviewDigest16>:<humanCopyRevision>"`. Changes whenever anything visible changes. |
| `teamMode` | boolean | `WORK_STATE_TEAM_MODE=1`. |
| `story` | `{reviews, story, groups} \| null` | Ledger progress reviews, the build story, group count. |
| `refresh` | object \| null | Contents of `refresh.json`. |
| `source` | object | `{kind, mode:"read-only-sqlite", connected, pollIntervalMs, lastCheckedAt, lastUpdatedAt, error, stale}`. |
| `copyRevision` | number | Human-copy revision. |
| `rulesFile` | `{path, instructionsPath, approvedCount, loadedInClaudeCode}` | Paths use `~`. |
| `setup` | `{scan, work, extraction}` | Onboarding scan state (idle), five most recent groups, refresh step. |

`Request` fields: `id, conversationKey, conversationKeys, original{text,source,sourceId,url,promptNumber,atEpoch}, explicitRequestText, scopeUpdates[], projects[], agentIds[], items[], workstreams[], updatedAtEpoch, explicitRequestId, groupId, workProduct[], activity[], lifecycle, startedAtEpoch, progress (Review|null), completedAtEpoch, requestedBy(+Source), shipEstimate(+Source), stageSourceText, stageSource, afterShip, title, titleSource, sourceContentHashes[], contentFingerprint, review{checked,checkedAtEpoch,actor,available}, humanCopy{state,...}, goals?[]`.
`titleSource` is one of `title-cache`, `request-group`, `explicit-work-state-request`, `original-human-request`.
`humanCopy.state` is `current`, `outdated`, `pending` or `unavailable`.

`Agent` fields: `id, kind (session|recorded-owner|unassigned), label, platformSource, agentId, agentType, sessionId, contentSessionId, sessionTitle, recordedSessionStatus, project, projects, inCurrentScope, identityEvidence, presence{status: recent|quiet|unknown|finished, isLive, evidence, lastActivityAt, finishedAt?}, isSubagent, launch, work[], activity[] (<=8), counts{work,open,done}, canMarkFinished`.
`presence.status` is `recent` when the last activity is within 15 minutes, else `quiet`; `finished` when a stop was recorded at or after the last activity.

### `GET /api/work-view/events` — server-sent events
Headers `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`. Frames:

```
retry: 1000

event: work-view
data: <full snapshot JSON>

event: heartbeat
data: {"at":"<ISO>","source":{...}}
```

`work-view` is sent on connect and whenever `[revision, source.connected, source.error, setup]` changes
(polled every `ALETHEIA_POLL_MS`). `heartbeat` every 15 s. The original also sends `setup-scan`, `setup-state`
and `setup-import` while its onboarding runs; the clone never does.

### `GET /api/work-view/evidence/:kind/:id`
`kind` is `work-state`, `observation`, `prompt`, `summary`, `session` or `tool-use`; `id` a positive integer.
Returns `{kind, ...row}` (columns in [02](02-data-model.md)), `404 {"error":"Recorded evidence not found."}`,
or `400 {"error":"Invalid id"}`. Tool input and response are cut to 4000 characters.

### `GET /api/work-view/file/:kind/:id/:index`
Serves a deliverable file recorded in an observation (`files_modified[index]`) or a work-state entry
(`work_product` list item `index`). Only when the path is absolute, has no `..`, has an allowed extension
(images, video, pdf, docx, pptx, key, xlsx, csv, html) and exists as a regular file.
Headers: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts`.

### `POST /api/work-view/review`
Body `{requestId: string(1..2000), expectedFingerprint: 64 hex, checked: boolean}` (no other keys).
`200` returns the new snapshot.
`404` unknown request. `409 {error, snapshot}` when the fingerprint is stale ("This work changed...") or when
checking a request not reported complete. `503` when the source is disconnected or review storage is down.

A request is **reported complete** when its review shows `percent == 100` (and, if an explicit lifecycle
exists, the review was checked at or after it), or its explicit lifecycle says `complete: true` or a status in
`done, completed, complete, shipped, delivered, needs-review, review, in-review, awaiting-review, ready-for-review`.

### `POST /api/work-view/rules`
Body `{action, ruleId?, rule?}`; `rule` is `{scopeTier: everywhere|project|situation, scopeName (<=80), when (<=300), then (1..600, trimmed)}`.

| action | needs | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `add` | `rule` | new owner rule `own_<hex>`, status `on` |
| `edit` | `ruleId`, `rule` | change scope, when, then |
| `approve` | `ruleId` (`rule` optional) | learned -> approved, status `on` |
| `turn-on`, `turn-off` | `ruleId` | only for rules with status `on` or `off` (else 409) |
| `replace` | `ruleId`, `rule` | new rule; old gets status `replaced`, `replacedBy`, `replacedAt` |
| `dismiss` | `ruleId` | status `dismissed` (an owner rule then disappears) |
| `restore-suggestion` | `ruleId` | only `pref_*` rules (else 409): blanks the saved fields so the suggestion shows again |

A project or situation rule needs a non-blank `scopeName` (400). An unknown rule is 404.
`200` returns the snapshot, after rewriting `MY-RULES.md` and notifying event clients.

### `POST /api/work-view/agents/mark-finished`
Body `{agentGroupId}`. Only for a subagent (`isSubagent`, with `agentId` and `contentSessionId`) that
`canMarkFinished`; else `409`. Appends an `agent-lifecycle` entry with `stop_source: "owner-marked-finished"`.

### `POST /api/work-view/rules/load-in-claude-code`
Rewrites `MY-RULES.md` and, unless a line equal to `@<rules path>` already exists, appends that line to the
instructions file (adding a newline first when the file does not end in one). Idempotent. Returns the snapshot.

### `POST /api/work-state/entries`
Used by `save_goals.py`. Body `{cwd: string, list: string(1..200), fields: object}`. `fields` has at least
one key; values are string, boolean, finite number or `null`; keys non-empty; at most 2000 characters as JSON.
`list = "my-rules"` is refused (`403`). Plain-text reply `Saved to "<list>" in <project>.` where `<project>`
is the project key of `cwd`. The clone writes to the overlay store.

### Setup
`GET /api/setup/state` always returns `{status:"complete", ...}`. `GET /api/setup/scan` returns the idle scan
state. Every `POST /api/setup/*` returns `404 {"error":"Account setup is not part of aletheia-mem."}`. The
original's onboarding (choice of local or hosted memory, checkout, history import) is account and billing
flow with no meaning here.

## 3.3 Behaviour not guaranteed identical

The exact wording of validation errors (the original uses zod) and the 404 HTML body are reproduced from
observation, not from source.

## 3.4 Team mode

Team routes serve the same store as [31-team.md](31-team.md). `/v1/team/*` needs `Authorization: Bearer <sync token>`;
a read needs any valid token and a write needs `sync` or `admin`. `/api/hub/team/*` is the guarded local Hub route
and acts as the local operator. Bodies are JSON; `team_id` accepts a numeric id or the team name.

| Route | Method | Who | What |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/team` | GET | member | the caller's teams, role and projects |
| `/v1/team` | POST | valid token | create a team; the caller becomes its owner (`{name}`) |
| `/v1/team/projects` | GET | member | named projects (`?team_id=`) |
| `/v1/team/projects` | POST | owner | add `{team_id, project}` |
| `/v1/team/members` | GET | owner | members, roles, projects and revoked state |
| `/v1/team/members` | POST | owner | `{team_id, name, role, projects[], token_id?}`; mints a sync token when `token_id` is absent and returns it once |
| `/v1/team/members/revoke` | POST | owner | `{team_id, member_id}`; also revokes that member's sync token |
| `/v1/team/shares` | POST | owner | `{team_id, member_id, projects[]}` replaces a member's project shares |
| `/v1/team/board` | GET | member | pins and decisions (`?team_id=&project=`) |
| `/v1/team/board` | POST | editor/owner | `{team_id, project, kind: "pin"\|"decision", text}` |
| `/v1/team/memory` | POST | editor/owner | `{team_id, project, kind?, title?, text, source_type?, source_id?}` |
| `/v1/team/brief` | GET | member | `{team, project, text, facts[], decisions[], sourceIds[]}` (`?team_id=&project=&days=&maxChars=`) |
| `/v1/team/search` | POST | member | `{team_id, query, project?, limit?}`; results respect project ACLs |
| `/v1/team/leave` | POST | member | tombstones the caller's shared rows, removes its shares and revokes its token |
| `/v1/team/audit` | GET | owner | append-only team actions (`?team_id=&limit=`) |

Failures: `401` for a missing, revoked or expired token (`member_revoked`, `token_revoked`); `403` for the wrong
role or a project the member does not share (`viewer_read_only`, `project_forbidden`, `not_member`); `404` for an
unknown team, member or project; `400` for a duplicate team name, the last owner, or a malformed body.

The store check is the gate: `TeamStore.authorize()` runs for the HTTP route, the CLI and a direct store call.
A route cannot bypass it, and a test calls the store directly to prove that.

## 3.5 Erasure

These routes are the guarded local UI/admin path. The CLI is `aletheia erase ...`; both call the same modules.

| Route | Method | What |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/hub/erasure/report` | POST | `{project?, ids?: ["memory:12"], before?}` returns `{plan}` with counts and ids. Reads only; deletes nothing. |
| `/api/hub/erasure/apply` | POST | the same selector plus optional `export_path` and `receipt_path`; writes a pre-erase bundle, deletes the rows, purges the matching sync entities and writes an HMAC-signed receipt |
| `/api/hub/erasure/verify` | POST | `{receipt: <object>}`; `200 {ok:true}` or `400 {ok:false, reason}` |

`before` is an epoch or an ISO date and means `created_at_epoch < before`. `ids` accepts `12` (memory #12) or
`memory:12`, `fact:12`, `observation:12`, `episode:12`. A plan follows provenance: a memory's episode, its
observation, the facts on that observation/episode, and the summaries, keys, links, dismissals and review rows
that point at them. `apply` removes the hub rows and their FTS entries, the vectors, the device replica/outbox
when one is local, and asks the sync store for a purge, which drops every op body and leaves a tombstone
with a null payload. The receipt records counts and ids, never text; it is signed with
`HMAC-SHA256` over the key-sorted body with the local key at `~/.aletheia/erasure.key` (mode 0600).

An erasure of an offline device's copy is not possible from here: revoke its token and wipe the device. An
E2EE account cannot be matched by project or content id, so pass the entity ids explicitly or purge on the
device that holds the key.

## 3.6 Alerts

The guarded local UI/admin path. The CLI is `aletheia alerts ...`. Events: `device.paired`, `token.revoked`,
`quota.hit`, `sync.error`, `extraction.failed`, `queue.depth`. A rule either appends one JSON line to a local
file or POSTs to a webhook. A webhook body is signed with `X-Aletheia-Signature: sha256=<hex>` (HMAC-SHA256 over
the exact body) when the rule has a secret.

| Route | Method | What |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/hub/alerts/rules` | GET | every rule; the secret is reported only as `hasSecret` |
| `/api/hub/alerts/rules` | POST | add a rule: `{name, event, target: "webhook"\|"file", url?, path?, secret?, countThreshold?, minValue?, windowS?, rateLimitS?, allowPrivate?, enabled?}` |
| `/api/hub/alerts/rules/:id` | PATCH | update any of those fields |
| `/api/hub/alerts/rules/:id` | DELETE | remove one rule |
| `/api/hub/alerts/feed` | GET | deliveries, newest first (`?limit=`) |
| `/api/hub/alerts/test` | POST | `{id}` queues one test delivery for that rule and delivers what is due |
| `/api/hub/alerts/run` | POST | deliver every due row once |
| `/api/hub/alerts/check` | POST | read queue depth and extraction failures, emit those events, queue matches |

Delivery rules: `countThreshold` N waits for N events in `windowS`; `minValue` gates a numeric event such as
`queue.depth`; `rateLimitS` allows one delivery per rule per window. A 2xx is final; 5xx/429, a timeout or a
network error retries with exponential backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, ..., capped at 60 s) up to five attempts; other
4xx and a refused target fail immediately. A webhook target that resolves to a private, loopback or link-local
address is refused unless the rule sets `allowPrivate`. A name that does not resolve is refused (fail closed).
`sync.error` fires from the sync server's 500 path; `device.paired` from a successful join; `token.revoked` from
`/v1/sync/revoke`; `quota.hit` when a push hits a quota; `extraction.failed` and `queue.depth` from the
extraction worker. An alert store or delivery failure never takes the server or the queue down.

## 3.7 Requests, goals, story and economics

The universal `/v1` API also answers the Work views. These routes are read-only except for dismiss/restore and the
rule decide actions. Every number comes from a stored row; an empty store returns empty arrays and `empty: true`.
Full field descriptions and real samples are in [32-requests.md](32-requests.md).

| Route | Method | What |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/work/requests` | GET | request list; `?project=&filter=all\|needs-you\|shipped&sort=needs-you\|newest\|most-progress&group=agent\|tool` |
| `/v1/work/requests/:id` | GET | one request plus where it came from (sessions, prompts, facts) |
| `/v1/work/story` | GET | shipped / working / waiting counts, shipping velocity, learned habits |
| `/v1/work/goals` | GET | goal roll-up: Stalled / Moving / Nothing on it, aggregate progress, no-goal bucket, open asks |
| `/v1/context/economics` | GET | per-observation read tokens and work tokens |
| `/api/hub/requests/:id` | POST | `{action: "dismiss" \| "restore"}` |
| `/api/hub/rule-suggestions` | GET | suggestions with strength, dated quotes and decided counts |
| `/api/hub/rule-suggestions/:id` | POST | `{action: "approve" \| "edit" \| "reject" \| "restore", text?}` |
| `/api/hub/rules/:id/toggle` | POST | `{enabled: boolean}` |
| `/api/hub/rules/:id/replace` | POST | `{then, when?, scopeTier?, scopeName?}`; the old rule gets `replacedBy` and `replacedAtEpoch` |
| `/api/hub/rules/learning-run` | GET, POST | read the last learning run, or run `suggestRules` and record it |
| `/api/hub/rules` | GET | every rule with `createdAtEpoch`, `source`, `evidence`, `last_confirmed_epoch`, `age_days`, `stale` and `reasons`; `?stale=1` keeps flagged rules, `?older_than_days=N` keeps rules last confirmed more than N days ago |
| `/api/hub/rules` | POST | add a rule; optional `evidence: [{kind: "memory" \| "fact", id}]` (ids must exist) |
| `/api/hub/rules/:id/confirm` | POST | "this rule is still right": sets `last_confirmed_epoch` to now and writes an audit row; `{restore: epoch}` puts an earlier date back (the Undo) |
| `/api/hub/rules/diff` | GET | per tool file, rules only in the store, only in the file, or worded differently, with file and line; `?tools=a,b&projectDir=/abs/path`; read-only |

The CLI equivalents: `aletheia context economics [--project p] [--limit n]` and `aletheia rules suggest`.

### Session start context format

`/v1/context`, `/api/hub/context`, `aletheia context`, the `session_start_context` MCP tool and the SessionStart
hook all return the same context block. Its shape is controlled by the Hub setting `context.format`:

| Value | Shape |
|---|---|
| `index` (default) | Pinned and recent memories as one compact line each (id, time, type marker, title <= 100 chars, no narrative), grouped by day and first file; then session requests, active facts and rules. A legend, a fetch-more hint and a measured context-economics line close the block. |
| `classic` | The previous flat list: one line per memory with a date, type and a 160-character narrative snippet, then facts and rules. |

The setting is stored in the Hub settings table (`context.format`, value `"index"` or `"classic"`). The untrusted
wrapper, pinned-first order, the active-facts section, flagged-rule notes and the `maxChars` cut are the same in both
formats.

The active-facts section is further controlled by `context.facts` (`"auto"` default, `"on"`, or `"off"`), stored
under `ui.settings.context.facts`. `auto` lists only pinned, provider-extracted, or confidence ≥ 0.6 facts; `on`
keeps the historical behaviour; `off` hides the section.

### Rule dates, evidence and the re-check flag

Every rule keeps the date it was made, its source, the memories and facts it rests on (its evidence) and the date it
was last confirmed. A rule approved from a suggestion copies the suggestion's source ids and dated quotes as its
evidence; a rule added through the API or the `add_rule` MCP tool may name evidence ids. A rule made before this
existed has no evidence and keeps working.

A rule is flagged for re-check when any of these holds. The flag is computed on every read and is **a flag, never a
deletion**: a flagged rule stays enabled, keeps syncing and is never edited or removed. A synced rules file and the session context append `[re-check: <reasons> Verify before applying.]` to a flagged rule, so an agent that receives the rule also receives the warning. Confirming the rule removes the note on the next sync.

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `evidence_fact_superseded` | an evidence fact was superseded or closed after the rule was last confirmed |
| `evidence_fact_expired` | an evidence fact's `valid_to` or expiry passed after the rule was last confirmed |
| `evidence_memory_dismissed` | an evidence memory was dismissed after the rule was last confirmed |
| `newer_fact` | a newer active fact states a different object for the same project, subject and predicate as an evidence fact |
| `review_overdue` | no confirmation for more than the review window: setting `rules.reviewDays`, 7 to 730, default 90 |

A rule with no evidence can only be flagged by `review_overdue`. Each reason is `{code, message, evidence?}`. Confirming
a rule (`POST /api/hub/rules/:id/confirm`, `aletheia rules confirm <id>`, or the `confirm_rule` MCP tool) sets
`last_confirmed_epoch` to now, so a change that happened before it no longer counts. To stop following a rule, use
the existing turn-off route (`aletheia rules retire <id>` does the same): the rule is kept, not deleted.

`?older_than_days=N` also works on `GET /api/hub/memories` and in the `POST /v1/search` body (and as `older_than_days`
in the `search` MCP tool), so pruning old memories is a query. Memory rows already carry their date, `tool`,
`session_id`, `origin` and `files`.

---

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/compare/aletheia-vs-claude-mem.html

# claude-mem alternative: Aletheia compared with claude-mem


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) is a free, local memory and rules hub for AI coding tools, and a possible claude-mem alternative if you want one store shared by several hosts. This page compares it with claude-mem, the larger and older project, and says where each one is ahead. Aletheia is not affiliated with or endorsed by the claude-mem authors or Anthropic.

## Short answer

claude-mem is the bigger, more mature project. It has a far larger community, more features and more integrations. Choose it if Claude Code is your main host and you want its live viewer, its file read gate, its cloud sync option or its community.

Aletheia is a small alpha project. Choose it if you want one SQLite store that several hosts read over MCP, REST or the CLI, rules written once and synced into each host's own instruction file, and facts that record when they were true. Both projects run on your machine and both are Apache-2.0.

The two can run side by side. You can also copy your claude-mem memories into Aletheia.

## Facts about claude-mem, fetched 2026-10-29

These numbers come from GitHub and from claude-mem's own documentation. They change over time, so check the sources.

- Licence: Apache-2.0. Source: `gh api repos/thedotmack/claude-mem` and the repository README, https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem, 2026-10-29.
- Repository created: 2025-08-31. Source: the same `gh api` call, 2026-10-29.
- Stars: 104,569. Forks: 9,229. Source: the same `gh api` call, 2026-10-29.
- Contributors: 297, counted from the pages of `gh api repos/thedotmack/claude-mem/contributors` (anonymous contributors are excluded), 2026-10-29.
- Latest release: v15.6.0, published 2026-10-29. Source: `gh api repos/thedotmack/claude-mem/releases/latest`.

For scale, the Aletheia repository's first commit is dated 2026-10-26 and its first release, 0.1.0, is dated 2026-10-27 ([CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)).

## Where claude-mem is ahead

Every item below is stated in claude-mem's documentation. Aletheia's status for the same item is in the second half of each line.

- **Community and maturity.** The numbers above are claude-mem's. Aletheia's repository is days old and has one maintainer. Its real-tool evidence comes from one user on one machine. See [Status and limits](../project/status-and-limits.md).
- **A live viewer.** claude-mem's "My Work" page runs at the local worker URL, usually `http://localhost:37777`. It gathers recorded requests, progress and finished results and reads the saved memory database. Source: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/my-work.md, 2026-10-29. Aletheia has its own web interface, described in [The dashboard](../start/dashboard.md). It is newer and has had less use.
- **A file read gate.** claude-mem blocks Claude Code from reading a whole code file of at least 32 KB when that file already has observations, and offers an outline or a line range instead. It is on by default and fails open. Source: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/file-read-gate.md, 2026-10-29. Aletheia has a gate module (`src/hub/smart-file.mjs`) covered by tests. No hook or MCP tool calls it and it is off by default, so you cannot use it yet.
- **Many integrations.** The installation page lists Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Antigravity CLI and OpenClaw, and the README adds T3 Code, Pi and DeepSeek Harness. Sources: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation.md and https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem, 2026-10-29. Aletheia has hook adapters for six hosts and MCP plus rules for a seventh. Hooks ran in real sessions of Claude Code (two days of use), Command Code (one short session) and Codex CLI (one interactive session), one user on one machine. See [Tools overview](../tools/overview.md).
- **Cloud sync.** claude-mem offers an optional, paid cloud sync through cmem.ai Pro. It replicates the memory database across your devices. Its docs warn that observation narratives and full prompt text go to the sync hub. Source: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/cloud-sync.md, 2026-10-29. Aletheia Sync is self-hosted and free, and it has only been tested on loopback. See [Sync](../29-sync.md).
- **Vector search.** claude-mem's `search` tool matches by meaning first and then by keywords when its Chroma vector index is running. Source: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools.md, 2026-10-29. In Aletheia, vectors need an optional package, so a default install searches by keyword only. See [Search](../concepts/search.md).
- **More features around memory.** Its introduction page lists knowledge agents, a mode system, 28 languages and folder context files. Source: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/introduction, 2026-10-29. The README also lists TeamBrain, a shared workspace. Source: https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem, 2026-10-29. Aletheia has some counterparts, such as modes, an output-language setting, folder context files and a self-hosted team mode ([Team mode](../31-team.md)). This page does not claim parity with any of them.

## Where Aletheia differs

Each point is backed by Aletheia's code or README.

- **A tool-neutral store.** One SQLite store holds memories from every host, tagged with the host name. Any host reads it over MCP (stdio and HTTP), a REST API under `/v1` or the CLI. Source: the interfaces table in the [README](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/README.md).
- **Rules sync to many instruction files.** You write a rule once. `aletheia rules sync` writes it into the instruction file of each host in the registry, for example `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, a Cursor `.mdc` file and a Windsurf rules file. The registry has ten entries ([`src/hub/tools.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/tools.mjs)). Your own text outside the managed block is left alone ([`src/hub/rules-sync.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/rules-sync.mjs)). claude-mem also writes `CLAUDE.md` files, but its docs describe them as folder context with activity timelines, not as rules you author. See [Rules](../concepts/rules.md).
- **MCP, REST and CLI.** The MCP server exposes 13 tools, listed in [MCP tools](../reference/mcp-tools.md). The REST API and the CLI cover the same store.
- **Facts with two time axes.** A fact stores when it was valid (`valid_from_epoch`, `valid_to_epoch`) and when the hub recorded or expired it (`recorded_at_epoch`, `expired_at_epoch`). The `fact_history` tool answers "what was true on this date" with its `as_of` argument. Sources: [`src/hub/store.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/store.mjs) and [`src/hub/mcp-tools.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/mcp-tools.mjs). See [Facts and contradictions](../33-facts.md).
- **A benchmark gate.** CI fails a change that loses more than one point of Recall@5 on a seeded synthetic corpus ([`bench/gate.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/bench/gate.mjs), [workflow](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml)). It runs on Linux only. See [Benchmarks](../project/benchmarks.md).
- **Loopback only by default.** The server binds `127.0.0.1` unless you set `ALETHEIA_HOST`. A non-loopback bind turns on a login ([`src/config.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/config.mjs), [`src/server.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/server.mjs)).
- **No telemetry.** The README states there is no account, no telemetry and no network call unless you configure a model provider. A text search of `src/` and `bin/` for telemetry, analytics, PostHog and Sentry finds only a comment that says "No telemetry". claude-mem's docs say its anonymous usage analytics are on by default and can be turned off with `npx claude-mem telemetry disable`. Source: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/telemetry.md, 2026-10-29.

## Measured numbers

Retrieval only. The numbers show whether the evidence for a question is in the top five results. They are not answer accuracy, and answer accuracy is not measured.

On the LoCoMo dataset, 1,536 questions with gold evidence, raw dialogue turns stored as memories:

| System | Recall@5 | MRR |
|---|---|---|
| claude-mem 15.2.0, as shipped | 36.0% | 0.285 |
| Aletheia, keyword search (BM25) | 55.3% | 0.482 |
| Aletheia, keyword plus vectors (hybrid) | 57.4% | 0.497 |

All three rows are measured-by-us. Re-run the Aletheia rows with `bun scripts/compare-bench.mjs`. The command reads the JSON files in `bench/results/2026-10-26/` and needs no network. The claude-mem row comes from the README table and from `bench/claude-mem-baseline.mjs`. [Benchmarks](../project/benchmarks.md) has every command and the full table.

Read these numbers with five caveats.

1. The claude-mem run used version 15.2.0. The latest release on 2026-10-29 is v15.6.0, and the number was not re-run on it.
2. claude-mem is built to ingest through its language-model observer. The baseline saved raw turns through its save endpoint, which is the closest model-free equivalent. A run through the observer could score differently.
3. claude-mem's docs say its semantic matching uses Chroma only when the index is running. The committed files do not record whether it was running. Source: https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools.md, 2026-10-29.
4. The raw output of the claude-mem run is not committed in `bench/results/`. The README row records Recall@5, MRR and latency, and `scripts/compare-bench.mjs` does not print it.
5. The Aletheia hybrid row needs the optional embeddings package. Latency numbers are not like for like. Aletheia's figure is the mean time of the in-process ranking call, and it leaves out the time to embed the question. claude-mem's figure is an HTTP request to its worker, with p50 1,699 ms and p95 2,824 ms over 40 idle queries.

## Using both

Aletheia and claude-mem can run side by side. They use separate data directories, `~/.aletheia` and `~/.claude-mem` by default, and separate ports. Aletheia never writes to claude-mem's database. The importer opens it read-only with `PRAGMA query_only` ([`src/hub/importers.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/importers.mjs)).

claude-mem describes itself as injecting relevant context into future sessions (the repository description, 2026-10-29), and Aletheia's `SessionStart` hook for Claude Code prints a context block. If both are installed on one host, expect two context blocks. This page does not claim a tested combination. Run `aletheia install claude-code` without `--write` first to see every file it would change.

## Migrating

To copy your claude-mem memories into Aletheia, run:

```bash
aletheia import claude-mem
```

The command reads observations, session summaries and prompts and adds them to the hub. Add `--path <db>` for a database in another place and `--no-prompts` to skip prompts. The step-by-step guide is [Migrate from claude-mem](../guides/migrate-from-claude-mem.md).

## Licence and attribution

Aletheia is Apache-2.0. A few files come from claude-mem 15.2.0, also Apache-2.0: the optional legacy viewer, two skill prompts, some scripts and one derived module. [NOTICE.md](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/NOTICE.md) lists each file and the change made.

## Next steps

- [Migrate from claude-mem](../guides/migrate-from-claude-mem.md) - copy your memories into the hub.
- [Benchmarks](../project/benchmarks.md) - every command behind the numbers on this page.
- [Memory tools compared](memory-tools.md) - Aletheia against Mem0, Zep, Supermemory and Basic Memory.
- [Status and limits](../project/status-and-limits.md) - what has and has not been checked.

---

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/compare/memory-tools.html

# Memory tools compared: Aletheia, Mem0, Zep and Graphiti, Supermemory, Basic Memory


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) is a free, local memory and rules hub for AI coding tools. This page compares it with four other memory projects: Mem0, Zep with its open-source Graphiti framework, Supermemory and Basic Memory. It says what each project's own pages state, with a URL and a date, and it says when another tool is the better pick.

Every fact about another project was read from the URL beside it on 2026-10-29. Where a page did not say, the cell reads `UNVERIFIED`. A README that does not mention a feature is not proof that the feature is missing.

## The comparison at a glance

| | Aletheia | Mem0 | Graphiti and Zep | Supermemory | Basic Memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Licence | Apache-2.0 | Apache-2.0 | Graphiti: Apache-2.0. Zep is a managed commercial service | MIT | AGPL-3.0 |
| Runs on your machine | Yes | Yes, open-source library or Docker stack | Graphiti: yes, with a graph database. Zep: `UNVERIFIED` | Yes, `npx supermemory local` | Yes |
| Hosted or paid option | None | Managed platform | Zep, managed | Hosted platform | Cloud, price stated in its README |
| MCP | stdio and HTTP | Hosted server only | Reference server in the Graphiti repository | Open-source server, hosted at a URL | Yes |
| REST API | Yes, under `/v1` | Yes, open-source server and platform API | Reference service in the Graphiti repository | SDKs; REST reference `UNVERIFIED` | `UNVERIFIED` |
| CLI | Yes | Yes | None described for Graphiti | Starts the local server | Yes |
| Rules written into host instruction files | Yes | None described | None described | None described | `UNVERIFIED` |

The Aletheia column comes from the repository. See [Rules](../concepts/rules.md) and [MCP tools](../reference/mcp-tools.md). The other columns are explained in the sections below.

## Mem0

- Licence: Apache-2.0. Source: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0 and `gh api repos/mem0ai/mem0`, 2026-10-29.
- Local use: the open-source version runs as a library or a Docker stack on your own servers. Source: https://docs.mem0.ai/introduction, 2026-10-29.
- A model provider is needed. The README names OpenAI's `gpt-5-mini` and `text-embedding-3-small` as defaults. The open-source REST server needs an OpenAI key and a `JWT_SECRET`, and you create a local admin on your own server, not a Mem0 account. Sources: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0 and https://docs.mem0.ai/open-source/features/rest-api, 2026-10-29.
- Hosted option: a managed platform at app.mem0.ai with API keys. The README gives no prices. Source: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0, 2026-10-29.
- MCP: the documented server is hosted by Mem0 and stores memories in your Mem0 account. The page says nothing runs on your machine and describes no local MCP server. Source: https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/mem0-mcp, 2026-10-29.
- REST and CLI: the open-source REST server is a FastAPI service, and the docs index lists a separate platform API reference. The README describes a CLI that adds and searches memories. Sources: https://docs.mem0.ai/open-source/features/rest-api, https://docs.mem0.ai/llms.txt and https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0, 2026-10-29.

## Zep and Graphiti

- Graphiti is an open-source framework for temporal knowledge graphs. Licence: Apache-2.0. Source: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti and `gh api repos/getzep/graphiti`, 2026-10-29.
- Zep is a commercial, managed context layer built on Graphiti, and it runs its own graph database service. Sources: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti and https://help.getzep.com, 2026-10-29.
- Graphiti is self-hosted. It needs a graph database (Neo4j, FalkorDB or Amazon Neptune) and an LLM provider, and OpenAI-compatible local servers such as Ollama can be used. The README warns that smaller models may fail ingestion. Sources: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti and https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/getting-started/overview, 2026-10-29.
- Self-hosting the Zep server itself: `UNVERIFIED`. The help site does not say. The Graphiti README mentions a deployment in your own cloud. The `getzep/zep` repository describes itself as examples and integrations, so this page does not treat Zep as open source.
- Temporal model: both pages describe bi-temporal tracking and fact invalidation. These are the project's own claims.
- MCP and REST: the Graphiti README says the `mcp_server` and `server` folders are reference implementations, not production deployments, with no authentication. The help page for Graphiti did not describe an MCP server, so the two sources differ. Sources: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti and https://help.getzep.com/graphiti/getting-started/overview, 2026-10-29.

## Supermemory

- Licence: MIT. Source: https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory and `gh api repos/supermemoryai/supermemory`, 2026-10-29.
- Local use: "Supermemory local" is a single server binary started with `npx` or an install script. It listens on `localhost:6767` and uses a local embeddings model by default. The README says URL ingestion relies on a hosted reader service, so fully offline use has limits. Source: https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory, 2026-10-29.
- Hosted option: a hosted platform with a docs site and dashboard. The README states no prices. `UNVERIFIED` for pricing.
- MCP: an open-source server, available at a hosted URL, with the tools `memory`, `recall` and `context`. Source: the same README, 2026-10-29.
- REST: the README lists npm and Python SDKs. A REST endpoint reference is `UNVERIFIED`.
- The documentation site did not load. Fetches of https://supermemory.ai/docs, https://supermemory.ai/docs/intro and https://docs.supermemory.ai failed on 2026-10-29, so every Supermemory fact here comes from the README.

## Basic Memory

- Licence: AGPL-3.0, stated for both the local and cloud versions. Source: https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory and `gh api repos/basicmachines-co/basic-memory`, 2026-10-29.
- Local use: notes are Markdown files on your disk with a local SQLite index. Source: https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory, 2026-10-29.
- Hosted option: the README states a cloud version at $15 a month with a 7-day free trial. Source: the same README, 2026-10-29.
- MCP and CLI: both are described in the README. Connected hosts named there include Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and VS Code.
- REST: the README mentions an API server only in passing and has no endpoint reference. `UNVERIFIED`.
- Rules files: the README does not describe writing rules into host instruction files. Aletheia's own README table of 2026-10-26 recorded "partial (AGENTS.md)" for Basic Memory, and the 2026-10-29 README does not confirm it. `UNVERIFIED`.
- Import: the README lists Claude conversations, ChatGPT exports and memory JSON files.

## Benchmark claims

Each vendor publishes its own numbers. Aletheia's numbers are retrieval only (Recall@5) and are measured by us. See [Benchmarks](../project/benchmarks.md).

- Mem0 reports 92.5 on LoCoMo, 94.4 on LongMemEval and 64.1 on BEAM at 1M tokens, vendor-claimed. It says the scores reflect the managed platform, and that open-source users should expect "directionally similar gains but not identical numbers." Source: https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0, 2026-10-29.
- Supermemory claims first place on LongMemEval, LoCoMo and ConvoMem, vendor-claimed. It also presents an open-source framework, MemoryBench. Source: https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory, 2026-10-29.
- The Graphiti README gives latency figures with no benchmark data or method, vendor-claimed. Source: https://github.com/getzep/graphiti, 2026-10-29.

None of these numbers can be set beside Aletheia's Recall@5. The pages above do not give the metric, the model or the settings in a way that matches ours. Do not read a gap in either direction into them.

## Which to pick

- **You want a managed memory service for a product you build.** Use a hosted option: Mem0's platform, Zep or Supermemory's hosted platform. Aletheia is not a hosted service and has no managed cloud.
- **You need a knowledge graph over many sources.** Graphiti and Zep are built for that. Aletheia keeps entity rows and has a graph retrieval channel that is off by default and was measured only on a synthetic test ([CHANGELOG 0.1.4](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)).
- **You want a team service run by someone else.** The projects above offer hosted options. Aletheia's team mode and sync are self-hosted, and they have not been tested across two real machines. See [Team mode](../31-team.md).
- **You keep your notes as Markdown files you read and edit yourself.** Basic Memory stores them that way. Aletheia stores memories in SQLite and exports them as JSONL or Markdown.
- **You use several coding hosts and want one local store and one set of rules.** This is the case Aletheia was built for. Check [Tools overview](../tools/overview.md) for what has been verified on a real install.
- **You already use claude-mem and it works for you.** Stay with it. See [Aletheia and claude-mem](aletheia-vs-claude-mem.md).

## Next steps

- [Aletheia and claude-mem](aletheia-vs-claude-mem.md) - the closest comparison, with measured numbers.
- [Claude Code memory options](claude-code-memory.md) - how Aletheia fits next to CLAUDE.md and auto memory.
- [Status and limits](../project/status-and-limits.md) - what is verified and what is not.

---

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/compare/claude-code-memory.html

# Claude Code memory options: CLAUDE.md, auto memory, MCP servers and Aletheia


Claude Code starts every session with a fresh context window, and it carries knowledge between sessions with two built-in mechanisms: CLAUDE.md files that you write and auto memory that Claude writes. Aletheia (aletheia-mem) is a local memory and rules hub that sits beside them. It adds a memory store that other hosts can read too, and it writes a managed block of rules into your `CLAUDE.md` without touching the rest of the file.

Every statement about Claude Code on this page comes from Anthropic's documentation and was fetched on 2026-10-29. The URL is next to each statement.

## Persistent memory in Claude Code, in short

- Put rules and project facts you want in every session into a `CLAUDE.md` file. You write it, Claude reads it.
- Let auto memory keep the small notes Claude picks up from your corrections. It is built in and needs no install.
- Add an MCP server when Claude needs to read or write data in another system, such as a memory store.
- Use hooks or a plugin when something must run at a point in the session, such as loading context at the start.
- Add Aletheia when you want one memory store and one rule list shared by Claude Code and other hosts.

## CLAUDE.md files

A `CLAUDE.md` file is a Markdown file of persistent instructions. Claude reads it at the start of every session. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, 2026-10-29.

The same page lists these locations, from the broadest scope to the narrowest:

| Scope | Location |
|---|---|
| Managed policy | `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md` on Linux and WSL, with other paths on macOS and Windows |
| User | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` |
| Project | `./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md` |
| Local | `./CLAUDE.local.md` |

What else the page says:

- Files in the directory tree above the working directory are loaded at launch. Files in subdirectories load when Claude works with a file there. All found files are concatenated, not overridden.
- The page says to aim for under 200 lines per file, because longer files use more context and reduce how well Claude follows them. Claude treats the file as context, not as enforced configuration.
- A `CLAUDE.md` can import other files with `@path/to/file`, to a depth of four hops.
- Rules can be split into `.claude/rules/` files, and a rule can be limited to some paths with a `paths` field.
- `/init` writes a starting `CLAUDE.md`. `/memory` lists and opens the memory files. `/context` shows which ones loaded.
- Block-level HTML comments are stripped before the content reaches Claude.

### AGENTS.md

Claude Code can read `AGENTS.md` as project instructions from version 2.1.277. By default it does so only when there is no `CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` in the working directory or above it. If both exist, Claude reads the `CLAUDE.md` files only, unless the `CLAUDE.md` imports `AGENTS.md` or you change the **Project instructions** setting in `/config`. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, 2026-10-29.

## Auto memory

Auto memory is notes that Claude writes for itself. Source for this whole section: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, 2026-10-29.

- It is on by default in local sessions. Turn it off with the toggle in `/memory`, with `autoMemoryEnabled` in settings, or with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`.
- Each project has a folder at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`. It holds a `MEMORY.md` index and one file per topic.
- The first 200 lines or 25 KB of `MEMORY.md` load at the start of each session. Topic files load on demand.
- The notes are plain Markdown that you can read, edit or delete. They are machine-local and are not shared across machines.
- Claude records four kinds of notes: `user`, `feedback`, `project` and `reference`.

## MCP servers

MCP is an open standard for connecting AI tools to other systems. The Claude Code docs say MCP servers give it access to tools, databases and APIs. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, 2026-10-29.

- Add a local server with `claude mcp add [options] <name> -- <command> [args...]`, or a remote one with `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>`.
- Scopes are local (the default), project (a `.mcp.json` file you can commit) and user (`~/.claude.json`, every project).
- Claude Code warns when one tool result is over 10,000 tokens and caps it at 25,000 by default.
- The docs tell you to trust a server before connecting it, because a server that fetches outside content can carry prompt injection.

An MCP memory server is one that stores and returns memories through these tools. Aletheia has one: 13 tools, listed in [MCP tools](../reference/mcp-tools.md). An MCP server gives Claude tools to call, such as a memory search. Loading context at the start of a session is the job of a hook.

## Plugins and hooks

A plugin is a directory of skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers that Claude Code installs as one unit, usually from a marketplace. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins, 2026-10-29.

A hook is a command that Claude Code runs at a point in the session. A `SessionStart` hook can return `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, and Claude Code inserts it as a system reminder at the start of the conversation. The other events include `UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop` and `SessionEnd`. Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, 2026-10-29.

Hooks are how a memory tool loads context without waiting for Claude to ask, and how it captures what happened. Aletheia is not a Claude Code plugin. Its installer edits your settings files directly. See below.

## Where Aletheia fits

| Mechanism | Who writes it | Where it lives | How it reaches Claude |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLAUDE.md | You | Files on disk | Loaded at session start |
| Auto memory | Claude | `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` | Index loaded at session start |
| Aletheia managed block | You, in the hub | Inside `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or a project `CLAUDE.md` | Loaded as part of that file |
| Aletheia memory store | Hooks and you | `~/.aletheia/hub.db` | `SessionStart` hook and MCP tools |

Aletheia does not replace either built-in mechanism. It does not read or write the auto memory folder, and a search of `src/` and `bin/` for `MEMORY.md` finds nothing. It can read Claude Code session transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/` to back-fill memories, read-only, with `aletheia import transcripts claude-code`.

Install it for Claude Code with:

```bash
aletheia install claude-code          # dry run: lists every file, writes nothing
aletheia install claude-code --write
```

On a throwaway home directory, the dry run printed this. Paths are shortened to `~`, and `...` marks two lines left out.

```
Claude Code (claude-code) — full, mcp-verified
  write  mcp      ~/.claude.json  (mcpServers.aletheia)
  write  hooks    ~/.claude/settings.json  (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd)
  write  rules    ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md  (1 rule)
  ...
Dry run: nothing was written. Add --write to apply.
```

What has been checked on a real Claude Code:

- MCP server listed by the real CLI on 2026-10-27: Claude Code 2.1.312.
- Hooks ran in real sessions of Claude Code (two days of use), Command Code (one short session) and Codex CLI (one interactive session), one user on one machine.

Nothing here shows that an answer was better with Aletheia than without it. Answer accuracy is not measured. See [Benchmarks](../project/benchmarks.md) and [Claude Code setup](../tools/claude-code.md).

## How the managed block coexists with your own text

Aletheia writes its rules between two HTML comment markers, `<!-- aletheia:rules:begin -->` and `<!-- aletheia:rules:end -->`. Everything outside the markers is yours and is not changed ([`src/hub/rules-sync.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/src/hub/rules-sync.mjs)). Each write to an existing file keeps a timestamped backup of the old file.

A real run, with a temporary home directory and a `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` that held a heading and one sentence of the user's text. Paths are shortened to `~`.

```bash
aletheia rules add "Run the test suite before committing."
aletheia rules add "Use two-space indents" --when "editing JavaScript"
aletheia rules sync --tools claude-code --global           # dry run
aletheia rules sync --tools claude-code --global --write
```

```
- claude-code: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — 2 rules, would change (add --write)
- claude-code: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — 2 rules, written (backup ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.aletheia-2026-10-29T19-49-03-236Z.bak)
```

The file after the write:

```
# My notes

Always answer in short sentences.

# Rules

Managed by aletheia-mem. Edit them in the Rules page; this block is rewritten on sync.

## Everywhere

- Run the test suite before committing.
- When editing JavaScript: use two-space indents
```

Then the user added a line below the block, a third rule was added and the sync ran again. The new rule appeared inside the block and the user's line stayed where it was.

Things to know:

- **Edit rules in the hub, not in the block.** The block is rewritten on every sync. Text you type between the markers is replaced.
- **Sync is a file write.** A rule reaches Claude Code when the sync writes it. Claude Code loads `CLAUDE.md` files at the start of a session, so expect the change in the next session. Running `aletheia rules sync` without `--write` shows the change first.
- **The markers are HTML comments.** The Claude Code docs say block-level HTML comments are stripped before the content is injected, so the markers should not use context. That was not checked in a live session.
- **Mind the 200-line guidance.** The block adds a heading, a sentence and one line per rule to a file that Claude reads in full. Keep rules short.
- **Remove it cleanly.** `aletheia uninstall claude-code --write` removes only the entries its install manifest lists. In a separate temporary-home run, the `CLAUDE.md` went back to the user's heading and sentence.
- **AGENTS.md is a different file.** `aletheia rules sync` writes `AGENTS.md` for Codex, Command Code and OpenCode and writes `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code. Per the Claude Code docs, a project that has both is read through the `CLAUDE.md` only. Sync both files, or import `AGENTS.md` from your `CLAUDE.md`.

## Next steps

- [Rules](../concepts/rules.md) - how rules are stored, scoped and synced.
- [Write rules once](../guides/write-rules-once.md) - a short guide to the sync command.
- [Session-start context](../concepts/session-context.md) - what the `SessionStart` hook sends to Claude Code.
- [Claude Code setup](../tools/claude-code.md) - install, verify and uninstall for this host.
- [Aletheia and claude-mem](aletheia-vs-claude-mem.md) - the other memory plugin for Claude Code.
