Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/project/benchmarks.html

# Aletheia benchmarks: how to reproduce every published number


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) publishes retrieval numbers only. They show whether the evidence for a question is among the top five search results. They are not answer accuracy, and answer accuracy is not measured. This page lists the command behind each published number, what the command does, the results with dates, and the experiments that did not work.

## What is and is not measured

Measured, retrieval only:

- Recall@k and MRR on the LoCoMo dataset, against Aletheia's own search and against a claude-mem worker.
- Search latency and database size on a synthetic store of 50,000 rows.
- A synthetic Recall@5 and p95 latency that CI checks on every change.

Not measured:

- Whether a model gave a correct answer. There is no published reader-and-judge run.
- Retrieval on your own memories, in other languages, or in long real sessions.
- The claude-mem Chroma index, unless it was running during the claude-mem baseline. The committed files do not say.
- Sync, remote MCP and team mode.

Every number below is `measured-by-us`, with the command. None is a vendor claim.

## The five commands

| Command | What it measures | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `bun bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs` | Recall@1 to 15, MRR and time per query on LoCoMo, for several search strategies | The dataset file. The optional embeddings package for vector rows |
| `bun bench/claude-mem-baseline.mjs` | The same questions against a running claude-mem worker | An isolated claude-mem worker |
| `bun bench/scale.mjs 50000 20000 --index tuned --queries 200 --seed 1` | Insert rate, keyword search latency, synthetic Recall@5 and database size at 50,000 rows | Nothing |
| `bun bench/gate.mjs` | Synthetic Recall@5 and p95 latency, checked against `bench/baseline.json` | Nothing |
| `bun scripts/compare-bench.mjs` | Prints the LoCoMo table from the committed result files | Nothing, no network |

Quick check that needs no setup:

```bash
bun scripts/compare-bench.mjs
```

It reads `bench/results/2026-10-26/*.json` and prints one row per strategy, then compares each earlier claim with the measured value. On 2026-10-29 every row of the claim table read `REPRODUCED`, which means within 0.5 points of the earlier claim.

## Reproduce the LoCoMo numbers

LoCoMo is a dataset of ten long conversations with questions and gold evidence. The script header names the source, https://github.com/snap-research/locomo. The download URL below answered HTTP 200 to a HEAD request on 2026-10-29. This page did not download it again. Check your copy against the SHA-256 that every result file records.

1. Download the dataset into `bench/data/`. The folder is ignored by git.

   ```bash
   mkdir -p bench/data
   curl -o bench/data/locomo10.json https://raw.githubusercontent.com/snap-research/locomo/main/data/locomo10.json
   sha256sum bench/data/locomo10.json
   # 79fa87e90f04081343b8c8debecb80a9a6842b76a7aa537dc9fdf651ea698ff4
   ```

   On 2026-10-29 the author's local copy had that SHA-256.

2. Install the optional embeddings package in a folder of its own. Vector and rerank rows need it. Keyword rows do not. The first run downloads the models once.

   ```bash
   mkdir -p bench/runtime && cd bench/runtime
   bun add @huggingface/transformers    # the 2026-10-26 runs used 4.3.1
   cd ../..
   export ALETHEIA_TRANSFORMERS_FROM=$PWD/bench/runtime
   ```

   The embedding model is `Xenova/bge-small-en-v1.5` (384 dimensions, quantised). The reranker is `Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2`.

3. Run one row. These are the exact commands recorded for the 2026-10-26 results:

   ```bash
   bun bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs --data bench/data/locomo10.json --facts none --out bench/results/2026-10-26/raw-turns.json
   bun bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs --data bench/data/locomo10.json --facts dataset --out bench/results/2026-10-26/dataset-facts.json
   bun bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs --data bench/data/locomo10.json --facts dataset --rerank --out bench/results/2026-10-26/dataset-facts-rerank.json
   bun bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs --data bench/data/locomo10.json --limit 3 --facts dataset --rerank --out bench/results/2026-10-26/dataset-facts-3-rerank.json
   bun bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs --data bench/data/locomo10.json --facts rules --out bench/results/2026-10-26/our-facts-rules.json
   ```

   Use a new output folder for your own run, then pass it to `bun scripts/compare-bench.mjs <folder>`.

### How the LoCoMo benchmark works

The method is in [`bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs).

- Each conversation gets its own in-memory store. Every dialogue turn is saved as one memory, and the conversation id is the project, so a question only searches its own conversation.
- Questions of LoCoMo categories 1 to 4 that have gold evidence are used. That is 1,536 questions over 10 conversations. Category 5 is left out.
- Recall@k is the share of a question's gold evidence turns found in the top k results, averaged over questions. MRR is the mean of 1 divided by the rank of the first gold turn.
- The strategies are `and-prefix` (the first shipped search, where every word must match), `bm25` (any word may match, with stemming), `dense` (vector cosine), `hybrid` (BM25 and vectors fused by reciprocal rank fusion), `hybrid+facts` and `hybrid+facts+rerank` (the top 30 candidates reordered by a cross-encoder).
- Facts are extra search keys that point back to the turn they came from. `--facts dataset` uses the facts that the LoCoMo authors wrote. Aletheia did not produce them. `--facts rules` uses Aletheia's own rule extractor. `--facts provider` asks a local model.
- `ms/query` is the mean time of the in-process ranking call. It leaves out the time to embed the question. For the rerank rows it is the cross-encoder time for one question only.

## Results

All rows are from `bench/results/2026-10-26/`, generated on 2026-10-26. The result files do not record the machine, the Bun version or the operating system, so latency columns cannot be compared across machines.

| Run | Questions | Recall@5 | MRR | ms/query |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude-mem 15.2.0 (as shipped), raw turns | 1,536 | 36.0% | 0.285 | p50 1,699 ms, p95 2,824 ms (idle, 40 queries) |
| Raw turns, keyword (BM25) | 1,536 | 55.3% | 0.482 | 2.00 |
| Raw turns, hybrid | 1,536 | 57.4% | 0.497 | 3.72 |
| Dataset facts, all 10 | 1,536 | 64.8% | 0.591 | 5.53 |
| Dataset facts, 3 conversations | 383 | 67.4% | 0.620 | 5.80 |
| Dataset facts, 3 conversations, + rerank | 383 | 73.9% | 0.686 | 251.16 |
| Dataset facts, all 10, + rerank | 1,536 | 72.3% | 0.680 | 646.19 |
| Rule-extracted facts, all 10 | 1,536 | 57.7% | 0.492 | 4.94 |

Notes on the table:

- The Aletheia rows come from `bun scripts/compare-bench.mjs`. The BM25 row was added from the same output.
- The claude-mem row comes from the project README. The raw output of that run is not committed in `bench/results/`. It was produced by [`bench/claude-mem-baseline.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/bench/claude-mem-baseline.mjs), which saves each turn through claude-mem's save endpoint and queries its search endpoint with a limit of 10. The date of that run is not recorded in a committed file.
- Latest claude-mem release on 2026-10-29 is v15.6.0 (`gh api repos/thedotmack/claude-mem/releases/latest`). The baseline used 15.2.0 and was not re-run.
- claude-mem is built to ingest through its language-model observer. Raw saves are the closest model-free equivalent, so the baseline does not show how claude-mem does through its normal path.
- The hybrid and rerank rows need the optional embeddings package. A default install without it searches by keyword only.
- Dataset facts are an experiment, not a feature. They show what good facts could add: about 7 points of Recall@5 over raw turns.

Compare the claude-mem row with the raw-turns rows only. They are the only rows where both systems store the same raw text. The speed columns are not like for like: one is an in-process call and the other is an HTTP request to a worker.

### The raw-turns numbers were re-run on 2026-10-31

The published 57.4% (MRR 0.497) comes from `raw-turns.json`, written on 2026-10-26. A local `raw-turns.log` that git ignores showed hybrid Recall@5 of 44.7%. The log is older than the JSON (file times 16:58 and 18:13 on 2026-10-26), so it comes from an earlier version of the search code, not from the published run.

Re-runs on 2026-10-31 with `bun bench/locomo-retrieval.mjs --facts none`, on a 12-core Linux machine:

| Code | Hybrid Recall@5 | MRR |
|---|---|---|
| commit `e6145b3` (the published run's commit) | 57.4% | 0.497 |
| commits `b2c5b3d`, `4bd5f54` | 57.4% | 0.497 |
| commits `11ef293`, `b843eb4`, `1e326b6`, `ddf442c` (before and after the redaction change) | 57.7% | 0.502 |
| current main, two runs | 57.7% | 0.502 |
| current main, one earlier run | 54.2% | 0.473 |

So the 57.4% reproduces exactly at the commit that produced it, and the current code scores 57.7%. Search changes since 2026-10-26 added 0.3 points; the redaction change did not affect the result. One run on 2026-10-31 scored 54.2% with keyword-only BM25 at 52.1% where the other runs give 55.2%. BM25 does not use the embedding model, so I could not explain that run and it did not repeat in three more runs. Treat it as an unexplained outlier. The README keeps the 2026-10-26 numbers, which `scripts/compare-bench.mjs` reproduces from the committed files.

## Scale: 50,000 rows

```bash
bun bench/scale.mjs 50000 20000 --index tuned --queries 200 --seed 1
```

The script builds a synthetic store with Zipf-like word frequencies and random unit vectors, from a seeded random generator. It measures insert rate, keyword search latency for all projects, one project and one project plus host, a synthetic Recall@5, database size, and vector search over 20,000 vectors. The script is [`bench/scale.mjs`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/bench/scale.mjs).

The README records, for this command on Linux: keyword search p95 of 32.7 ms for one project and 58.6 ms across all projects. It states a target of 50 ms and says the target is met for project-scoped search. The [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for 0.1.4 says the project-scoped p95 fell from 67.5 ms to 32.7 ms. This page did not re-run the command, because it takes long. Synthetic text is not real memory, so treat the figures as a check on the index, not a promise for your data.

## The regression gate

```bash
bun bench/gate.mjs
```

The gate builds a fixed synthetic corpus of 50,000 rows with seed 1, runs 100 queries and takes the median p95 of 5 passes. Each query has several near-duplicate distractors, so Recall@5 sits near 0.9 and has room to drop. It compares the result with [`bench/baseline.json`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/bench/baseline.json):

- It fails when Recall@5 drops by more than 0.01, one point.
- It fails when p95 latency rises by more than 20%, but only if the baseline p95 is at least 5 ms.
- It exits with an error if the baseline parameters do not match the run.

The committed baseline was written on 2026-10-28 on `linux x64 bun 1.3.10` at commit `343bb19`, with Recall@5 0.9 and p95 7.759 ms. CI runs the gate on Linux only ([workflow](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml)).

A run on 2026-10-29, on Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64 with Bun 1.3.10, took 9.8 seconds:

```
gate: recall@5 0.9000 (baseline 0.9000, delta +0.0000)
gate: p95 latency 8.688 ms (baseline 7.759 ms, +12.0%)
gate: PASS
```

Latency was 12% above the baseline and the gate still passed. Latency is noisy, so the gate guards against large regressions, not small ones.

## Other scripts in `bench/`

- `bench/graph-recall.mjs` is a synthetic test of the graph retrieval channel. It uses no model and no real data.
- `bench/accuracy.mjs` is an answer-accuracy harness with a fixed reader prompt and a blind judge. No result from a real model is published. Its retrieval arm ranks by word overlap, not by Aletheia's search, so a run of it would not measure Aletheia's retrieval.

## Negative results

These are the experiments that did not give the hoped-for result.

- **The rule extractor does not reproduce the fact gain.** Aletheia's rule-based extractor added 1,672 facts. Recall@5 moved from 57.3% to 57.7%, +0.4 points. The dataset's own facts added 7.3 points (57.5% to 64.8%). Files: `bench/results/2026-10-26/our-facts-rules.json` and `dataset-facts.json`.
- **The 1B local model run failed.** Ollama `llama3.2:1b` answered a trivial chat request with HTTP 200 in 2.92 seconds. The `facts-v1` extraction prompt over two LoCoMo turns returned HTTP 500 after 4 minutes 41 seconds. No fact was extracted, so no recall number from a local model is claimed. Source: [`provider-note.txt`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/bench/results/2026-10-26/provider-note.txt).
- **Adding neighbouring turns lowered Recall@5.** On the 3-conversation run, returning each top hit with its two neighbours gave 68.9% against 73.9% for the plain reranked list, and used more than twice the tokens.
- **Reranking is slow.** It lifted Recall@5 by 6.5 points on the 3-conversation run, and the cross-encoder took about 251 ms per question, against about 6 ms without it.
- **The first shipped search scores near zero.** The `and-prefix` strategy, where every word of a question must match, scored 0.1% on natural-language questions. It is kept as the before baseline.

## Next steps

- [Aletheia and claude-mem](../compare/aletheia-vs-claude-mem.md) - how the claude-mem row should and should not be read.
- [Search](../concepts/search.md) - how keyword, vector and rerank search work in the hub.
- [Status and limits](status-and-limits.md) - everything that is not verified.
- [Facts and contradictions](../33-facts.md) - how facts are extracted and gated.

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/project/status-and-limits.html

# Aletheia status and limits: alpha, what is verified and what is not


Aletheia (aletheia-mem) is alpha software: a free, local memory and rules hub for AI coding tools. The memory engine and the installers work in tests. A small number of real-tool checks have been done, by one user on one machine, and this page lists them in fixed wording so that nothing reads stronger than what was checked.

## Status in one paragraph

Aletheia is alpha. Expect rough edges, changes between 0.1.x releases and gaps in what has been tried on real tools. CI runs the test suite on Linux, macOS and Windows. Hooks have run in real sessions of three hosts, and the real CLI listed the MCP server for four. That evidence is thin. Answer accuracy is not measured. Benchmarks are retrieval only.

## What the tests cover

Run the whole suite with:

```bash
bun test
```

Tests are the main evidence for the memory engine and the installers. In particular:

- The MCP server was run against the official MCP SDK client for protocol versions 2025-11-25 down to 2024-11-05.
- Each installer is tested against fixtures in a temporary home directory. Each installed hook command is run end to end with a recorded payload.
- Rules files for Claude Code, Command Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenCode, Copilot and Aider are written and checked in temporary folders. The table is in [`docs/verification/rules-targets.md`](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/docs/verification/rules-targets.md). The Copilot and Aider formats were not re-checked against those tools' documentation.
- The Claude Desktop MCP config is merge-tested against a fixture. It has not been opened in the app.

A fixture test proves the file is well formed. It does not prove the real tool accepts it.

## What ran on real tools

These sentences are the only claims made about real tools:

- MCP server listed by the real CLI on 2026-10-27: Claude Code 2.1.312, Command Code 1.88.1, Codex 0.130.0, OpenCode 1.18.33.
- Hooks ran in real sessions of Claude Code (two days of use), Command Code (one short session) and Codex CLI (one interactive session), one user on one machine.
- Cursor, Gemini CLI and Windsurf: config written from docs, not tested on a real install. No hook ran in Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf or OpenCode.

In those sessions prompts and tool events were captured, secrets were redacted and the checker found no leaks. "Works with" is not claimed for any tool.

`aletheia install --list` prints the same status for every host. On 2026-10-29 it printed:

| Host | Level | Verification | Hook events installed |
|---|---|---|---|
| claude-code | full | mcp-verified | SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd |
| command-code | full | mcp-verified | SessionStart, PostToolUse, Stop |
| cursor | full | from-docs-only | sessionStart, beforeSubmitPrompt, postToolUse, afterAgentResponse, stop, sessionEnd |
| codex | full | mcp-verified | SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd |
| gemini-cli | full | from-docs-only | SessionStart, BeforeAgent, AfterTool, AfterAgent, SessionEnd |
| windsurf | full | from-docs-only | pre_user_prompt, post_run_command, post_write_code, post_cascade_response |
| opencode | mcp+rules | mcp-verified | none (MCP and rules only) |

`mcp-verified` means the real CLI listed the server. `from-docs-only` means the format came from the host's documentation and was tested against fixtures. See [Tools overview](../tools/overview.md) for each host.

## What is not verified

- Cursor, Gemini CLI and Windsurf have not been tried on a real install. No hook has run inside Cursor, Gemini CLI, Windsurf or OpenCode.
- Answer accuracy is not measured. Recall@5 is retrieval, not whether an answer was correct. There is no published reader-and-judge result.
- The 1B-model extraction run failed. Facts from Aletheia's own extractor were measured with the rule extractor only. See [Benchmarks](benchmarks.md).
- Sync and end-to-end encryption are tested with temporary data directories and a loopback hub. No real tunnel and no second host were used. See [Sync](../29-sync.md).
- End-to-end encryption covers payloads, not metadata such as device id, operation kind, entity id, timing or ciphertext size.
- Remote MCP delegates TLS to a reverse proxy or tunnel. OAuth is not built. See [Remote MCP](../30-remote-mcp.md).
- The graph retrieval channel is off by default. It was tested on a synthetic set and not on real data.
- The ten README translations are machine-translated. No native speaker has reviewed them.
- At 50,000 synthetic rows, keyword search p95 is 32.7 ms for one project and 58.6 ms across all projects. These numbers are synthetic and come from one Linux machine.

## Platform status

Aletheia needs Bun 1.1 or newer. The CLI runs on Bun, not Node.

| Platform | What is checked | What is not |
|---|---|---|
| Linux | The test suite, the install smoke test and the regression gate run in CI | Real-tool checks were done on one machine |
| macOS | The test suite and the install smoke test run in CI | The README records no real-tool trial on macOS |
| Windows | The test suite runs in CI | No real tool was tried. Several checks are skipped |

CI uses the GitHub `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest` and `windows-latest` runners with Bun 1.3.10 ([workflow](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml)). The regression gate runs on Linux only. `aletheia service install`, which sets up auto-start, is for Linux and macOS only, as its help text says.

The test files skip these checks on Windows, because they need a POSIX shell for hook commands or POSIX file modes (found by searching the test files for `skipIf(process.platform === "win32")` on 2026-10-29):

- the end-to-end install, hook, server, spool, doctor and uninstall test
- the end-to-end capture test for every full-capability host
- the memory pipeline test
- the test that no file is written into a project folder
- the hook-execution checks for Gemini CLI and Windsurf
- one temporary-folder cleanup check
- four file-permission checks

The README gives a shorter summary of these skips. This page follows the test files.

## Roadmap

No roadmap is published in the repository. The `[Unreleased]` section of the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) was empty on 2026-10-29. Open work is in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/issues). The gaps listed above are known gaps, not promises.

## Report from a real install

The most useful contribution is a report from a real install of a host that has only a config written from docs. The [contributing guide](https://github.com/mohamed-ashraf-elsaed/aletheia-mem/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) asks for an issue with:

1. The tool and its version.
2. The command you ran, for example `aletheia connect cursor --write` or `aletheia install cursor --write`.
3. What the tool did: did it list the MCP server, did a hook run, did the next session get memory back.

Run a dry run first. Without `--write` the command prints every file it would change and writes nothing. `aletheia doctor` prints server, hook and spool checks. Attach its output with secrets removed.

For Claude Code, Codex CLI and Command Code, the maintainer script `bun scripts/hook-check.mjs <data-dir> --tool <name>` opens the hub database read-only. It scans for redaction leaks and prints PASS or FAIL for each expected hook event. Use the "New host" issue form to ask for a host that is not listed.

# Dependencies

Aletheia has no required runtime dependencies. It uses the Bun standard library and Bun's built-in SQLite
binding only. The audit that enforces this is `scripts/audit-deps.mjs`:

```bash
bun scripts/audit-deps.mjs
```

The command fails when a required dependency is added without a written reason in the script's allowlist, or
when a listed licence is copyleft. Run it in CI and before a release.

## devDependencies

None. The project has no build step and no test-only packages; the test suite runs with `bun test` alone.

## Vendored code

Everything below is copied or derived from **claude-mem** 15.2.0, licensed under Apache-2.0. Attribution and
the exact change for each file is in [NOTICE.md](../NOTICE.md).

| Path | Licence | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| `public/work.html`, `public/assets/` | Apache-2.0 | claude-mem 15.2.0 (optional legacy viewer) |
| `prompts/request-progress/SKILL.md`, `prompts/owner-goals/SKILL.md` | Apache-2.0 | claude-mem 15.2.0 |
| `vendor/owner-goals/` | Apache-2.0 | claude-mem 15.2.0 |
| `src/ledger/commands.mjs` | Apache-2.0 | claude-mem 15.2.0 (derived) |

This project's own code is also Apache-2.0, per [LICENSE](../LICENSE).

# 1. Architecture

## What the original is

claude-mem is a memory plugin for coding agents. Its worker (`scripts/worker-service.cjs`, a 4.2 MB Bun
bundle) records every prompt, tool call, observation and session summary into
`~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db`, and serves several web pages. "My Work" is the page at `/`: a React
single-page app (Vite build in `ui/work-view/`) over a small JSON and server-sent-events API.

The worker listens on `37700 + (uid % 100)`. That is why this machine's instance is on `37700`
(uid 1000). The default `37777` appears only in help text.

Everything the page shows comes from three places:

| Source | Written by | Read by the page through |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-mem.db` tables `sdk_sessions`, `user_prompts`, `observations`, `session_summaries`, `tool_uses`, `work_state_entries` | claude-mem's hooks and the model it runs | `GET /api/work-view` |
| The **ledger**, files in `~/.claude-mem/work-view/` | an LLM "refresh" that runs inside the worker | `GET /api/work-view` |
| Small stores the page itself writes: review marks, saved rules, "agent finished" marks | the worker, on POSTs from the page | `GET /api/work-view` |

The page never calls anything else for its main view. It downloads one JSON document, the
**snapshot**, and then keeps it fresh over one event stream.

## Components of the clone

```
                      browser (public/ = original SPA)
                         |  GET /  GET /work-view/assets/*
                         |  GET /api/work-view     POST review | rules | mark-finished
                         |  GET /api/work-view/events   (SSE: work-view, heartbeat)
                         v
 +--------------------------- Bun process: bin/aletheia-server.mjs ------------------------------+
 |  server.mjs   routing, static files, guards (localhost only, same-origin JSON POSTs)    |
 |      |                                                                                  |
 |  app.mjs  WorkViewService --- snapshot() ---------------------------------------------+ |
 |      |        |  actions: review, saveRule, markAgentFinished, loadRulesInClaudeCode   | |
 |      |        |  SSE clients, 1 s change poll, 15 s heartbeat                          | |
 |      |        v                                                                        | |
 |      |   source.mjs SourceReader                                                       | |
 |      |        |  change detection -> rebuild only when something changed               | |
 |      |        |-- foldWorkState (readmodel/work-state.mjs)                             | |
 |      |        |-- readActivityRows + buildAgentView (readmodel/agent-view.mjs)         | |
 |      |        |-- buildRequests (readmodel/projection.mjs)  <- ledger (ledger/read.mjs)| |
 |      |        '-- hash of cited evidence rows                                          | |
 |      |-- humancopy.mjs   optional card text from an OpenAI-compatible model           | |
 |      '-- store/  overlay.db (own work-state log)   reviews.db (checked marks)         | |
 |                                                                                       | |
 |  refresh/auto-refresh.mjs  every 10 min: refreshNeeds() -> run job -> refresh.json    | |
 |      '-- orchestrator.mjs  goals -> grouping -> reviews -> alignment -> story          | |
 |            |-- providers.mjs  claude CLI | OpenAI-compatible HTTP                      | |
 |            |-- ledger/commands.mjs  validators + file writers (the original's CLI)     | |
 |            '-- vendor/owner-goals/*.py  export prompts, save goals                      | |
 +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
        |                                  |                          |
 claude-mem.db (read-only)       <ledgerDir>/ (read + write)    <dataDir>/ (read + write)
```

## One snapshot, step by step

`WorkViewService.snapshot()` (called per request and per poll):

1. `SourceReader.read()` computes cheap signatures: work-state head (count, max id, overlay head),
   activity head (max id and count of five tables, `PRAGMA data_version`), ledger file mtimes. If none
   changed, it returns the cached view.
2. If they changed, inside one read transaction it re-folds work state (when that changed), runs
   `readActivityRows` (bounded SQL), builds the agent view,
   and hashes every raw row each request cites.
3. `goalLinks()` attaches, to each request, the goals the alignment step linked it to.
4. The service adds, per request, a content fingerprint and the review state (checked or not).
5. `HumanCopy.observe()` annotates each request with `humanCopy` and queues generation if a provider is
   configured.
6. It adds `rulesFile` (path, approved count, loaded flag), `setup`, and the composite `revision`
   `"<agentRevision>:<digest of reviews>:<humanCopy revision>"`.

The event stream sends a full snapshot on connect and again whenever `revision`, `source.connected`,
`source.error` or `setup` change. A heartbeat every 15 s carries `{at, source}`.

## Why a clone and not the original

The original is wired into the worker: its routes, its database manager, its cloud sync and its onboarding.
The clone keeps the **contract** and replaces the wiring:

- It never writes to `claude-mem.db`. Entries the original appends there (rules, "agent finished", saved
  goals) go to the clone's own `overlay.db`, folded in with the source entries.
- It has no account, cloud sync, or onboarding. `/api/setup/state` always reports `complete`.
- The refresh gives the model its evidence inline and needs no tools, so any chat model works.

## Process model

One Bun process. Timers: change poll (only while a page is open), heartbeat (same), human-copy pump (1 s),
refresh check (10 min). The refresh runs inside the same process and shells out to `python3` (goal export
and save) and to the `claude` CLI when that provider is chosen. A refresh is single-flight: `refresh.json`
records `state: running` and the pid, and another process refuses to start while that pid lives.

---

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/02-data-model.html

# 2. Data model

## 2.1 Tables read from `claude-mem.db`

Opened with `readonly: true`, `PRAGMA query_only = ON`, `busy_timeout = 1500`. Every SELECT goes through a
helper that turns "no such table" and "no such column" into an empty result, so an older database still
renders (and so a wrong column name fails silently, see finding F1).

| Table | Columns used | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `sdk_sessions` | `id, content_session_id, memory_session_id, project, platform_source, user_prompt, custom_title, status, started_at_epoch, completed_at_epoch, cwd` | A **conversation** is `(platform_source, content_session_id)`. `memory_session_id` links to observations and summaries. |
| `user_prompts` | `id, session_db_id, prompt_number, prompt_text (first 1200 chars), created_at_epoch` | The human's asks. |
| `observations` | `id, memory_session_id, project, agent_id, agent_type, prompt_number, title, subtitle, type, files_modified, created_at_epoch` | Agent activity; files an observation modified (work product). |
| `session_summaries` | `id, memory_session_id, project, prompt_number, request, completed, next_steps, created_at_epoch` | A request's recorded outcome and next step. |
| `tool_uses` | `id, session_db_id, content_session_id, memory_session_id, project, platform_source, tool_name, tool_input, tool_response, prompt_number, agent_id, agent_type, cwd, created_at_epoch` | Work-state write attribution, subagent launches, commits, pushes, PRs, published documents. |
| `work_state_entries` | `id, project, list_name, fields (JSON), created_at_epoch, origin_device_id, origin_local_id, sync_rev` | The append-only log behind goals, rules, "agent finished", and agent-reported work items. |

`created_at_epoch` is milliseconds since 1970 everywhere.

### Bounds on every read

| Read | Bound |
|---|---|
| observations | newest 300 |
| session summaries | newest 100 |
| work-state write tool calls | newest 5000, only since the oldest of the 240 most recent work-state entries minus 5 s |
| sessions with a prompt in the last 14 days | 600, plus every session the ledger grouped |
| prompts of those sessions | newest 12000 |
| subagent launches (`Agent`/`Task` calls) | 2000 |
| work product calls and observations | 2000 each, since the same window start |
| work records shown | 240; recent activity 160 |

## 2.2 Work-state entries

An entry is `{project, list_name, fields}`. `fields.task` selects a **task** inside the list; without it the
fields apply to the **list** itself. Folding in order (by `created_at_epoch`, then device id, then
`origin_local_id`/`id` as BigInt): each field sets its value, and a `null` value deletes the field.
A task or list is **closed** when `fields.status` is `done` or `dropped` (case-insensitive).
A list is open when it has fields of its own (and is not closed) or any open task.

Reserved list names:

| List | Meaning | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `owner-goals` | The current goals. One task per goal (`Priority: <title>` or `Open ask: <title>`). | `save_goals.py` |
| `owner-goals/<YYYY-MM-DD>` | A past month's goals (history). | `save_goals.py --start --end` |
| `my-rules` | Saved rule state. One task per rule, `Rule: <ruleId>`. | the Rules actions |
| `agent-lifecycle` | "This subagent finished". One task per agent. | a stop hook, or "Mark finished" |
| anything else | Work reported by agents (a plan, a checklist). | agents, via the `work_state_write` tool |

Task fields the view understands (first non-empty wins, in this order):

| Meaning | Field names |
|---|---|
| request text | `request`, `human_request`, `user_request` |
| next step | `next_step`, `nextStep`, `next`, `next_action`, `remaining`, `pending`, `then_run` |
| outcome | `outcome`, `result`, `completed`, `verified`, `verification` |
| progress note | `human_summary`, `summary`, `progress`, `phase`, `stage`, `status_note` |
| owner | `owner` |
| explicit request id | `request_id` (task, else list) |
| lifecycle | `request_status` (string), `request_complete` (boolean) |
| requester / ETA / stage | `requested_by`, `requester`, `human_requester` / `ship_estimate`, `eta`, `target_ship_at`, `due_at` / `stage`, `phase` |
| after ship | `docs_url`, `documentation_url`, `promo_url`, `announcement_url`; `classification`, `category`, `tags`; `post_ship`, `after_ship` |
| work product | `work_product(s)`, `deliverable(s)` (JSON list or object), any field ending `_url` |

## 2.3 The overlay (`<dataDir>/overlay.db`)

Same shape as `work_state_entries` (`id, project, list_name, fields, created_at, created_at_epoch`).
Ids are stored as `OVERLAY_ID_BASE + rowid` with `OVERLAY_ID_BASE = 2^40`, so they never collide with source
ids, still sort after them, and evidence lookups can route by id (`>= 2^40` goes to the overlay).
Source rows and overlay rows are folded together.

## 2.4 The review store (`<dataDir>/work-view-reviews.db`)

```sql
CREATE TABLE work_view_reviews (
  request_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  content_fingerprint TEXT NOT NULL,
  checked_at_epoch INTEGER NOT NULL,
  actor TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (actor = 'local-user'));
```

A card is "checked" only while the stored fingerprint equals the card's current fingerprint. Any change to
the work it cites un-checks it.

## 2.5 The ledger (`<ledgerDir>/`)

All JSON, mode 0600, written atomically (temp file then rename). Formats are the original's exactly.

```
request-groups.json            { version:1, updatedAt, conversations:{<convKey>: groupId}, groups:{<groupId>: Group}, ignored:{<convKey>: reason} }
progress/g_<12hex>.json        Review (one per group)
story.json                     { narrative, preferences:[{preference, kind, supportCount, quotes:[{quote, at}]}], writtenAt }
alignment.json                 { links:{<groupId>:[{goal, evidence}]}, unaligned:[groupId], basis:{<groupId>: hash16}, goals:[goalKey], alignedAt }
refresh.json                   { state, reason, agent, startedAt, finishedAt, needs, result, error, nextAt, steps:[{step, agent, startedAt, finishedAt, groups?}], pid? }
agent-written-prompts.json     { promptIds:[...], updatedAt }   (optional; prompts an agent wrote)
owner-goals/<YYYY-MM-DD>/      scratch for the goals step (owner-prompts.md, owner-map.md, owner-goals.json)
agent-runs/<hex>/              scratch for one refresh run, removed when it ends
failed-answers/                raw model answers that failed validation twice
```

`Group` = `{ title (<=120), anchor (convKey), projectRoot, links:[Link], decidedAt, anchorAsk }`.
`Link` = `{ kind: shared-work-list|shared-request-id|agent-judgment, conversations:[>=2 of the group's], evidence }`.
`Review` = `{ groupId, state: shipped|in-progress|stalled|abandoned|unknown, percent 0-100, startedAt, shippedAt, lastActivityAt, summary (<=280), narrative (<=1200), milestones (<=12 of {at,text<=200,evidence[]}), preferences (<=10 of {kind,preference<=200,quote<=300,at}), outcome|null, evidence (<=20), reviewedThrough, reviewedConversations, checkedAt, changedAt, readings (<=20 of {at,percent}) }`.
`outcome` = `{ landed:{text<=400,at,evidence}, usage:{level in-use|some-use|no-evidence|unknown,text,evidence}, value:{level high|medium|low|unclear,text,evidence}, regressions (<=10 of {text,at,fixedBy,evidence}), changes (<=12 of {what,why,at,evidence}) }`.

### Identifiers

| Id | Form |
|---|---|
| conversation key | `JSON.stringify(["conversation", platform_source, content_session_id])` |
| group id | `"g_" + sha256(anchorConversationKey).slice(0,12)` (stable when later conversations join) |
| request id | `["overall-request", groupId]`, or the conversation key, or `["explicit-request", <root>, <request_id>]` |
| request key (one prompt) | `["request", platform, String(sessionDbId), promptNumber]` |
| agent id | `["session", platform, String(sessionDbId), agentId|"unidentified"]`; others `["owner"|"unassigned", project, owner, agentId]` |
| work-state list id | `[lowercase(project), listName]`; task id `[listId, taskName]` |
| rule id | owner rules `own_<12hex>`; learned rules `pref_<sha256(preference).slice(0,12)>` |
| project root | the project key before its first `/` (so worktrees of one repo share requests) |

### Alignment basis

`alignment.basis[groupId]` is `sha256(JSON{groupId,title,firstAsk[:400],state,percent,summary, conversations(sorted)}).slice(0,16)`.
A group is "unaligned" (due) when it has no recorded decision, when its basis changed, when a link points at a
goal that no longer exists, or when the goal set changed.

## 2.6 Other files

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `<dataDir>/MY-RULES.md` | The approved rules as markdown, rewritten after every rule action. |
| `<dataDir>/human-copy.json` | `{version:1, entries:{<requestId>:{fingerprint, copy, generatedAt, model, usage}}}`. |
| `<dataDir>/human-copy-usage.jsonl` | One line per model call. |

---

Source: https://aletheia.mohamedashrafelsaed.com/docs/06-frontend.html

# 6. Frontend

Aletheia has one app page at `/`. It is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript: no framework, no build step, no font file, no
CDN and no dependency. It works offline. The older claude-mem viewer is kept as an optional page; it is described at
the end of this file.

Screens (real captures of the running app on seeded demo data, labelled `?demo=1`; taken 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27 UTC):
